title: Ottocraft
welcome: Welcome to Ottocraft. You start in a normal Overworld with a torch, a coffee and a slice of toast. This guide covers the whole pack: SkyFactory 3's progression rebuilt for a normal world, Hexxit II's dungeons, creatures and gear, plus Create, the Twilight Forest and the Aether.
Do the next unticked goal: nothing in the recommended order needs something from further down.

Click a goal for its hints: why, steps, what to bring, portal and multiblock pictures and every recipe. Left-click any item for its recipes in JEI, right-click for its uses. Close the hints with x or by clicking the goal again.
At a crafting table, press G (or the book button) to open the guide over it. The + beside a recipe fills the grid; shift-click + for as many as you can make.

Most goals tick themselves when you craft, find, place or defeat what they ask; tick the rest with their box. Progress is shared by everyone on the server and saved with the world; hover a ticked box to see who did it.

goals.text: Gather wood and make a Crafting Table
goals.hint: Punch a tree for logs, turn them into planks, then put 4 planks in a 2x2 square.
goals.why: Almost every recipe needs the 3x3 crafting grid.
goals.tip: Press G with a crafting table open, then click + beside a recipe to fill the grid.
steps: Hold left-click on a tree trunk to break logs. Get 4 or more.
Open your inventory (E): 1 log in the 2x2 grid makes 4 planks.
Fill the 2x2 grid with planks for a Crafting Table. Place it and right-click it.
Make sticks (2 planks stacked) for tools. Plant the saplings that fall from leaves.

goals.text: Make a stone pickaxe and a furnace
goals.hint: Mine cobblestone with a wooden pickaxe. 8 cobblestone in a ring makes a furnace.
goals.why: Stone tools outlast wood. The furnace cooks food, smelts ore and makes charcoal for torches.
steps: Make a wooden pickaxe (3 planks over 2 sticks).
Dig down a few blocks anywhere to reach stone; mining it gives cobblestone.
Make a stone pickaxe, axe and sword with cobblestone.
Put 8 cobblestone in a ring for a furnace. Smelt logs into charcoal and make torches (charcoal over a stick).

goals.text: Make a bucket and carry water and lava
goals.hint: Three iron ingots in a V make a bucket.
goals.why: For farms, Nether and Aether portals, cobblestone generators, Ex Nihilo barrels and escaping lava. Water puts out fires and makes farmland; a lava bucket smelts 100 items.
steps: Smelt 3 raw iron into ingots (from caves, the next goals or village chests).
Craft a bucket: iron ingots in a V.
Fill it at any water. Fill a second bucket from a lava pool (careful).
Infinite water: dig a 2x2 hole and pour water into two opposite corners.

goals.text: Sleep through your first night in a bed
goals.hint: Three wool (from sheep) above three planks makes a bed. Sleeping also sets your respawn point.
goals.why: A bed skips the night (zombies, skeletons, creepers) and makes you respawn at home, not at world spawn.
steps: Collect three wool of the same color and three planks.
Craft a bed and place it in a lit, enclosed shelter with room above it.
Use the bed at night to sleep and set your respawn point.

mobs.where: Spawns in most grassy Overworld biomes (Bamboo Jungle, Birch Forest, Cherry Grove, Dark Forest and 13 more). Lead them home with wheat and breed two for more.

goals.text: Hang a Hammock to rest during the day
goals.hint: Comforts hammocks hang between two ropes on facing walls; right-click a rope with Hammock Cloth to string it up.
goals.why: Sleep through the day without moving your bed spawn: handy before night-only mob hunts.
steps: Craft Hammock Cloth and two ropes.
Place one rope on each of two facing walls with a two-block gap, then right-click a rope with the cloth to hang the hammock.
Use the hammock during the day to rest until night. Keep a bed for your home respawn point.

goals.text: Recover your items from a Gravestone after dying
goals.hint: When you die, a gravestone keeps your items where you fell. Right-click or break it to get them back.
goals.why: The gravestone holds everything you dropped at death until you break it.
goals.tip: Some modded hazards can still destroy a grave: don't test it with valuable gear.
steps: Find where you died: the obituary or the JourneyMap death marker.
Bring food and tools, clear the area, then break the gravestone.
Check you got all your equipment back.

goals.text: Open your map and save a waypoint at home
goals.hint: Press J for the JourneyMap map. Press B to create a waypoint where you stand.
goals.why: Villages, structures and portals are far apart. A home waypoint always leads you back.
goals.tip: Several mods use B: fix key conflicts in Controls.
steps: Press J to open JourneyMap, or find its fullscreen-map binding in Controls.
Open Waypoints, create a waypoint at your base and name it Home.
Check its dimension and visibility settings.

goals.text: Claim your base chunks so they are protected
goals.hint: Open the FTB Chunks map (M) and drag across chunks to claim them for your team.
goals.why: Claimed chunks are safe from other players and explosions. You can force-load them later so machines keep running.
steps: Press M to open the FTB Chunks claim map.
Left-click and drag over the chunks around your base to claim them.
Invite friends to your team (FTB Teams) so they can build there too.

goals.text: Go limp as a ragdoll and get back up
goals.hint: Press H to flop over as a physics ragdoll; press Shift to stand up again.
goals.why: Sable Ragdolls turns you into a physics body for laughs, airship falls and screenshots. You keep your items.
goals.tip: Hard impacts hurt like falling: not near cliffs or lava. Blood Magic's Sigil of Holding also uses H: rebind one in Controls.
steps: Press H (rebind in Options > Controls > Sable Ragdolls). You keep your momentum.
Hold W, A, S or D to roll while limp.
Press Shift to stand up (after about 3 seconds).
Friends can grab and drag your ragdoll with the mouse buttons shown on screen.

goals.text: Apply the Settler Decree to a Bounty Board
goals.hint: Open a Bounty Board, click the Settler tab on the left and place the decree in the empty slot: the page opens for good with Age 1 jobs.
goals.why: Opens the Settler page: Age 1 jobs (items and kills) that pay one notch ahead. Optional: bounties never gate progression.
goals.tip: Right-clicking the board with the decree also works. Breaking the board returns it and every decree on it. The goal ticks when anyone opens the page.
steps: Craft the Settler Decree: a Bounty Board (kept), 2 paper, 2 ink sacs, a feather and a gold nugget (shape: ink, feather, ink / paper, board, paper / gold nugget).
Right-click a Bounty Board to open it and click the Settler tab (left edge).
Place the decree in the empty slot on that page. The page opens for good and gets 3 jobs at once, then a new one about every 3 minutes (up to 9).

goals.text: Optional: finish three Settler bounties
goals.hint: Bounties are side jobs, never a gate. Apply the Settler Decree to its page on a Bounty Board and hand in three jobs.
goals.why: Craft the Settler Decree (Bounty Board, kept, + 2 paper, 2 ink sacs, a feather and a gold nugget); later decrees arrive when the next age opens. Its page offers Age 1 jobs (items and kills from every strand) that pay one notch ahead, never a skip. Skip a job you don't like and the board offers a new one.
steps: Craft a Bounty Board (6 planks + 3 paper) or use one in a village, and place it. The Bounty Boards page explains how jobs work.
Apply the Settler Decree to its page on the board (the goal before this one).
Hand in three bounties; this goal counts them for you.
goals.tip: Lost your decree? Craft a copy: decree + paper (you keep the original). Old capstones still make their decree.

goals.text: Cook a meat skewer
goals.hint: Two pieces of raw meat on a stick make a skewer; cook it in a furnace or on a campfire.
goals.why: Cooks two pieces of meat at once and fills more hunger than one: a cheap travel meal.
steps: Put two raw meat (or fish) above a stick in the crafting grid.
Cook the skewer in a furnace or on a campfire.

goals.text: Open a Bird's Nest
goals.hint: Breaking leaves sometimes drops a Bird's Nest; right-click it for seeds, saplings and small treasures.
goals.why: Free seeds and saplings while you clear trees, before you have a sieve.
steps: Break leaves (or let them decay) around your base.
Right-click a Bird's Nest to open it.

obtain.birdsnests:birdsnest: Breaking leaves (and leaves that decay) sometimes drops a Bird's Nest.

goals.text: Find and read a Lost Book
goals.hint: Lost Books turn up in ruins, villages and dungeon chests and tell the story of each age.
goals.why: Each age has a short lore page: together they are the pack's story.
steps: Loot chests in ruins, villages and Battle Towers.
Read the book to learn where the next ring of the world starts.

obtain.lostbooks:random_book: Lost Books appear in dungeon, ruin and village chests and in the reward bag each player gets when an age opens.

goals.text: Find a biome with a Nature's Compass
goals.hint: Craft a Nature's Compass, choose a biome from its list and follow the needle.
goals.why: Villages, Battle Towers and the first ring of ruins need certain biomes. The compass points to the nearest biome you pick.
steps: Craft it: a compass ringed by saplings and logs.

goals.text: Break a Tumbleweed for a surprise
goals.hint: Tumbleweeds roll out of dead bushes in deserts and badlands; break one for a random item.
goals.why: Drops seeds, saplings, saddles, Lost Books, Hexxit trinkets and the odd diamond.
steps: Walk through a desert or badlands where dead bushes grow.
Hit a rolling tumbleweed to break it and pick up what it drops.

mobs.where: Tumbleweeds break loose from dead bushes in deserts and badlands and roll with the wind; at most one per player at a time.

goals.text: Tame a wild horse from Mo' Creatures
goals.hint: Mount a wild horse again and again until it stops bucking you off, then saddle it.
goals.why: Horses are the first travel upgrade: much faster than walking across the first ring, and a quick escape.
steps: Find a herd of wild horses on plains or savannas.
Right-click to mount one. It throws you off at first: keep remounting until hearts appear.
Put a saddle on it (saddles come from chests, fishing and tumbleweeds) and ride. Sneak-right-click a tamed horse to open its options.

mobs.where: Wild horses roam plains and savannas in herds. Mount one again and again until it stops throwing you off; hearts mean it is tamed.

goals.text: Wear Mo' Creatures hide or fur armor
goals.hint: Bears and big cats drop hide, foxes and goats drop fur: both make early armor.
goals.why: Leather-tier armor from hunting. Hide or fur also replaces leather in the basic Iron Backpack.
steps: Hunt bears, lions, tigers or panthers for hide; foxes, goats or raccoons for fur. They fight back.
Craft the pieces like leather armor.

goals.text: Craft a Stone Bow from More Bows
goals.hint: Stone bow: the first More Bows bow.
goals.why: A cheap early ranged weapon. Better bows (iron, gold, diamond, elemental) come with the same ages as armor.
steps: Craft a stone bow.

goals.text: Dodge out of danger
goals.hint: Press the Dodge key with a direction to roll away from an attack.
goals.why: A dodge makes you invulnerable for a moment: use it on creepers, skeleton volleys and boss slams.
steps: Bind the Dodge key in Options > Controls > Elenai Dodge if it has no key.
Hold a direction and press Dodge: you roll and take no damage for a moment.
Dodging needs some food in the hunger bar and has a short cooldown.

goals.text: Craft Wolf Armor for your dog
goals.hint: Craft leather wolf armor for a tamed wolf.
goals.why: Armor keeps your dog alive in caves, and dogs follow you through every age.
steps: Tame a wolf with bones.
Craft leather wolf armor and put it on from the dog inventory.

goals.text: Build faster with a Builder's Wand
goals.hint: A Builder's Wand extends the face of a wall or floor using blocks from your inventory.
goals.why: Builds walls, floors and bridges a whole row at a time.
steps: Craft a stone wand (cobblestone on two sticks); iron and diamond wands place more blocks.
Right-click the face of a block: matching blocks from your inventory extend that surface.
Press the Change Mode key (Controls > Better Builders Wands) to switch between row and surface modes.

goals.text: Hide a doorway with Camouflage Paste
goals.hint: Camouflage Paste copies the look of a block onto a secret door or wall switch.
goals.why: Hides entrances and chests from other players.
steps: Craft Camouflage Paste.
Right-click a secret door or switch with it while facing the block to copy.

goals.text: Twerk a Sapling into a Tree
goals.hint: Crouch repeatedly next to saplings and crops to make them grow (TS2K16).
goals.why: Free bonemeal while you wait for wood or food.
goals.tip: It can take a while. Saplings need light and clear space.
steps: Stand next to a sapling or crop.
Tap Shift quickly and repeatedly; green particles show it works.

goals.text: Use a Crook on leaves to get saplings and a Silkworm
goals.hint: Break leaves with a crook (sticks) for extra saplings and the odd silkworm.
goals.why: More saplings, and silkworms for renewable string.
steps: Craft a crook from sticks.
Break leaves with it: more saplings drop, and about 1 in 100 leaves drops a silkworm.

goals.text: Infest leaves with a Silkworm and crook them for string
goals.hint: Use a silkworm on leaves, wait until they turn white with webs, then break them with a crook.
goals.why: String for the sieve's String Mesh, wool, bows and fishing rods, without hunting spiders.
steps: Right-click a leaf block with a silkworm.
Wait until the leaves turn fully white (the infestation spreads).
Break the white leaves with a crook for string and sometimes more silkworms.

mobs.where: Spawns in the dark or at night in most Overworld biomes, The Beneath and the Twilight Forest (Highlands Underground, Spooky Forest, Underground). Spawners in dungeons and other structures.
Spawns in the dark in Sulfur Caves (Overworld) and The Beneath. Spawners in dungeons and other structures.

goals.text: Compost leaves or saplings in a Wooden Barrel to make Dirt
goals.hint: Right-click a wooden barrel with leaves, saplings or food. When full it slowly becomes dirt.
goals.why: Renewable dirt for farms and for sieving into seeds and pebbles.
steps: Craft a wooden barrel.
Right-click it with leaves, saplings, seeds, food or rotten flesh until full.
The compost turns into dirt. Right-click to take it out.

goals.text: Collect rain water in a Wooden Barrel
goals.hint: An empty wooden barrel left out in the rain slowly fills with water.
goals.why: Water before you have a permanent supply.
steps: Place an empty wooden barrel outdoors where rain reaches the ground (open sky above).
Wait for rain, then take the water with a bucket. In dry biomes or dimensions, fill it from a bucket.

goals.text: Craft a Sieve and a String Mesh
goals.hint: Sieve + String Mesh (9 string): right-click with gravel, sand or dust to sift.
goals.why: The heart of SkyFactory resources: gravel, sand, dust and dirt become ores, gems, seeds and pebbles.
steps: Craft the sieve and a string mesh (9 string).
Right-click the sieve with the mesh to insert it.
Right-click with gravel (or sand, dust, dirt), then keep right-clicking until it is sifted.
Sieves side by side all sift with one click.

goals.text: Craft a Hammer to turn Cobblestone into Gravel, Sand and Dust
goals.hint: Hammer cobblestone into gravel, gravel into sand, sand into dust.
goals.why: Turns endless cobblestone into everything the sieve needs.
steps: Craft a hammer.
Place cobblestone and break it with the hammer: gravel drops.
Hammer gravel for sand, then sand for dust.

goals.text: Sift Gravel, Sand and Dust in a Sieve for ore pieces
goals.hint: Sift gravel for ore pieces. 4 pieces = 1 ore chunk; smelt the chunk into an ingot.
goals.why: Renewable iron, copper, gold, lead, silver, nickel and aluminum, plus coal, diamonds, emeralds and lapis from gravel.
goals.tip: Press U on gravel, sand or dust in JEI for every drop and its chance.
steps: Sift gravel with a String Mesh or better.
Ore pieces drop by chance: iron, copper, gold, lead, silver, nickel, aluminum.
Craft 4 pieces of one metal into an ore chunk; smelt it into an ingot (or crush it for more).
Sand: more pieces and cactus seeds. Dust: redstone, glowstone, gunpowder, blaze powder. Dirt: seeds and pebbles. Crushed netherrack: cobalt and ardite.

goals.text: Make Clay by putting Dust into a water-filled Barrel
goals.hint: Fill a barrel with water first, then right-click it with dust.
goals.why: Clay for bricks, Tinkers grout, porcelain and the crucible, without finding a river.
steps: Fill a wooden barrel with water (bucket or rain).
Right-click it with dust from the hammer: it becomes a clay block. Right-click to take it.

goals.text: Explore a cave and return with coal, iron and copper
goals.hint: Mine coal, raw iron and raw copper in caves; smelt the raw metals.
goals.why: Iron makes tools, buckets, armor, hoppers and most machines. Coal fuels furnaces and torches.
goals.tip: Fortune gives extra raw ore. Iron is common at Y 16 to 64; deep caves also have diamonds.
steps: Bring torches, food, a stone pickaxe and spare blocks.
Light the cave paths you use.
Mine coal, raw iron and raw copper. Head back before supplies run low.
Smelt the raw metals in a furnace.

goals.text: Mine a whole ore vein at once with OreExcavation
goals.hint: Hold the Excavate key (default `, under Esc) and break one ore to mine the whole vein.
goals.why: Saves time and pickaxe swings on every ore vein and tree.
steps: Find an ore vein or a tree.
Hold the Excavate key and break one block.
Every connected block of the same kind breaks too. Each costs durability and a little hunger.

goals.text: Smelt iron and make a full set of iron tools
goals.hint: Iron pickaxe, axe, shovel and sword.
goals.why: An iron pickaxe mines diamonds, gold, redstone and many modded ores. Iron tools are fast and durable.
steps: Smelt about 10 raw iron into ingots.
Craft the pickaxe first (3 iron over 2 sticks), then the sword, axe and shovel.

goals.text: Wear a full set of iron armor and carry a shield
goals.hint: Helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots from 24 iron, plus a shield (planks and one iron).
goals.why: Armor more than halves the damage you take; a shield blocks arrows, creeper blasts and melee hits. You need both for caves and the Nether.
steps: Smelt 24 iron ingots (and 1 more for the shield).
Craft helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots.
Craft a shield and hold it in your off-hand (F swaps hands). Right-click to block.

goals.text: Upgrade your Sieve mesh and enchant it
goals.hint: Iron and diamond meshes give rarer drops; Fortune and Efficiency work on meshes.
goals.why: More and rarer drops (more diamonds, golden items). Fortune adds rolls; Efficiency sifts faster.
steps: Craft a flint mesh, then an iron, golden or diamond mesh.
Enchant it at an enchanting table or with books on an anvil.
Swap meshes for what you want: JEI lists the drops per mesh.

goals.text: Turn coal or charcoal into Mini Coal
goals.hint: 1 coal = 8 mini coal; each smelts exactly 1 item.
goals.why: A coal smelts 8 items; mini coal wastes nothing on small jobs.
steps: Put one coal (or charcoal) in the crafting grid for 8 mini coal.
Use one mini coal per item you smelt.

goals.text: Find a village and trade with a villager
goals.hint: Find a village (plains, desert, savanna, taiga, snowy plains) and right-click a villager with a job.
goals.why: Villages have food, beds and loot chests. Villagers trade books, tools and food for emeralds; emeralds also buy seeds at the Market.
goals.tip: Zombies kill or convert villagers (depends on difficulty): light and fence the village before night.
steps: Search plains, deserts, savannas, taigas or snowy plains.
Save a waypoint there (J, Waypoints).
Right-click an adult villager with a profession to see its trades.
Sell a crop or material it asks for to get emeralds. Protect villagers and their workstations.

mobs.where: Villagers live in villages (plains, desert, savanna, taiga and snowy plains). Get more by giving them beds and food (bread, carrots) so they breed, or cure a zombie villager with a splash potion of weakness and a golden apple.

goals.text: Set up a crop plot and bring animals back to your base
goals.hint: Hoe dirt next to water and plant seeds from grass. Hold wheat to lead cows and sheep home.
goals.why: Endless food, plus leather, wool and meat from breeding. Many mods also use wheat, carrots and potatoes.
steps: Break tall grass for wheat seeds.
Make a hoe and till dirt near water (water hydrates 4 blocks in every direction).
Plant the seeds; crops need light.
Hold wheat to lead cows and sheep. Fence them in and breed them (wheat on two adults).

mobs.where: Spawns in most grassy Overworld biomes (Bamboo Jungle, Birch Forest, Dark Forest, Forest and 11 more). Lead them home with wheat and breed two for more.

goals.text: Make a Watering Can
goals.hint: Hold right-click on crops to grow them faster. The reinforced can covers more.
goals.why: Speeds up crops and saplings around you.
steps: Craft a watering can and fill it at water.
Hold right-click while looking at crops or saplings.

goals.text: Speed up sugar cane with Snad
goals.hint: Plant sugar cane on Snad beside water: it grows faster than on dirt or sand.
goals.why: Snad speeds up sugar cane (plain sand does not).
steps: Craft Snad.
Place it beside water and plant sugar cane on it.
Keep the farm loaded with room above. Harvest the upper cane so it keeps growing.

goals.text: Harvest a wide area with a Scythe
goals.hint: A scythe cuts crops and grass in a large area per swing.
goals.why: Big fields in a few swings instead of one block at a time.
steps: Craft an iron scythe.
Swing at grown crops or tall grass: everything around breaks at once.

goals.text: Make a Cutting Board and a Pot from Pam's HarvestCraft
goals.hint: Pam's tools stay in the grid and cook hundreds of foods: press U on a tool in JEI.
goals.why: Pam's foods restore far more hunger and saturation than plain crops, and the tools are never used up.
steps: Craft the Cutting Board and the Pot. Also useful: Skillet, Saucepan, Bakeware, Mixing Bowl, Juicer.
Put the tool in the grid with the ingredients; the tool stays.
Press U on a tool in JEI for every food it makes.

goals.text: Cook a meal with Pam's HarvestCraft
goals.hint: Cook a meal with your Pam tools: apple pie, grilled cheese, noodle soup and more.
goals.why: Big meals keep you full for a long time.
steps: Gather ingredients from your farm, village gardens and Pam crops (wild gardens drop seeds).
Search the meal in JEI and press R for what it needs.
Craft it with the right tool in the grid.

goals.text: Trade at the Market for seeds and saplings
goals.hint: The Market sells seeds, saplings and Natura trees for emeralds.
goals.why: Seeds and saplings that are hard to find: Natura trees, Pam's crops, flowers.
steps: Craft the Market and place it.
Right-click it, browse the categories and pay with emeralds.

goals.text: Buy a Natura sapling from the Market
goals.hint: Natura's Overworld trees don't generate here: buy their saplings at the Market.
goals.why: Natura woods (maple, silverbell, amaranth, tiger) give unique planks and decorations.
steps: Open the Market and find the Natura saplings.
Buy one with emeralds and plant it like a normal sapling.

goals.text: Sift Topiary Grass to collect Natura saplings
goals.hint: Sift Topiary Grass for Natura Overworld saplings (Nether species: sift soul sand).
goals.why: Saplings for trees that don't generate in this pack.
steps: Craft Topiary Grass.
Sift it with a mesh its JEI sieve recipe accepts.
Plant and farm the saplings.

goals.text: Break grass to find Natura barley and cotton seeds
goals.hint: Break tall grass: Natura barley and cotton seeds drop at a low chance.
goals.why: Barley makes flour and bread; cotton makes string and wool.
steps: Break tall grass until barley and cotton seeds drop.
Plant them on farmland like wheat.

goals.text: Shear a sheep with Wooden Shears
goals.hint: Shears made from planks.
goals.why: Wool, leaves and vines before you have iron to spare.
steps: Craft wooden shears.
Right-click a sheep for 1-3 wool without killing it.

goals.text: Apply a block to a sheep with Shear Madness
goals.hint: Right-click a sheep with a full block to dress it in that block.
goals.why: Decoration: adult sheep wear the block, and shearing gives the block back.
goals.tip: No need to shear the sheep first. Some blocks have effects: TNT-covered sheep explode when killed.
steps: Find an adult sheep and hold a full, solid block.
Right-click the sheep with it.
Shear it to take the block back.

mobs.where: Spawns naturally in Bamboo Jungle, Birch Forest, Cherry Grove, Dark Forest and 13 more (the Overworld); Birch Forest, Cherry Grove, Dark Forest, Forest and 13 more (Fake Overworld); Birch Forest, Cherry Grove, Dark Forest, Forest and 13 more (Quarry). Lead them home with their favorite food and breed two of them to get more.

goals.text: Shear a block-covered sheep to restore its wool coat
goals.hint: Shear a block-dressed sheep to get the block back.
goals.why: The sheep then regrows normal wool for beds and banners.
steps: Craft shears (two iron ingots diagonally).
Right-click the dressed sheep with them: the block drops and the wool coat returns.

goals.text: Tame a Chocobo and saddle it
goals.hint: Feed a wild chocobo Gysahl Greens until hearts appear, then put on a Chocobo Saddle.
goals.why: Fast mounts that jump high; later colors swim, climb or fly. The Chocopedia explains breeding.
steps: Find wild chocobos in plains, savannas or forests, and Gysahl seeds in wild Gysahl gardens.
Grow Gysahl Greens and feed them to a chocobo until hearts appear.
Craft a Chocobo Saddle (saddle or leather + chocobo feather) and right-click to equip it.
Craft the Chocopedia (book, feathers, ink, lapis, gold) for colors and breeding.

goals.text: Pick Oreberries in a cave
goals.hint: Oreberry bushes grow in dark caves; their berries smelt into metal nuggets.
goals.why: Extra iron, gold and copper on cave trips; essence berries give XP.
steps: Look for small leafy bushes with colored berries in dark caves.
Right-click a ripe bush to pick the berries.
Smelt the berries into nuggets.

obtain.oreberries:iron_oreberry: Oreberry bushes grow in dark caves underground. Right-click a ripe bush to pick its berries.

goals.text: Store bulk items in Storage Drawers
goals.hint: A drawer holds 32 stacks of one item; a Drawer Controller links drawers into one inventory.
goals.why: Keeps cobblestone, dirt and ores out of your chests, and shows what is inside.
steps: Craft a drawer and place it with the front reachable.
Right-click the front holding the item to deposit; double-right-click deposits every matching item you carry.
Left-click the front to take one item; sneak-left-click takes a stack.
Add a storage upgrade when it fills. Label or lock drawers as needed.

goals.text: Build a Sophisticated Storage barrel or chest
goals.hint: Craft a Sophisticated Storage chest or barrel (needs a Storage Drawer) and add upgrades.
goals.why: Bigger, upgradable storage. Its recipes use a drawer in place of the lever, so it comes after Storage Drawers.
steps: Craft the storage block and place it.
Store items and put storage upgrades in its upgrade slots.
Check each upgrade's tooltip and JEI recipe first; backpack upgrades are a separate set.

goals.text: Craft a Charset Barrel and store items in it
goals.hint: A Charset barrel holds up to 4096 of one item and works with automation.
goals.why: A cheap bulk barrel for one item: cobblestone, seeds or wood.
steps: Craft the barrel.
Right-click with an item to store it; left-click takes a stack.
Hoppers and pipes can insert and extract.

goals.text: Craft a basic Iron Backpack
goals.hint: Wool and leather (or Mo' Creatures hide or fur) around a chest make the first backpack.
goals.why: More inventory for long trips. It is SkyFactory 3's backpack; the Sophisticated Backpack is crafted from it.
steps: Craft the backpack and right-click to open it.
Upgrades start from an Upgrade Core (string, paper, leather); JEI shows each upgrade.
Iron, gold and diamond tiers are crafted from the tier below.

goals.text: Carry a Sophisticated Backpack
goals.hint: Craft a Sophisticated Backpack from an Iron Backpack; it holds more and takes upgrades.
goals.why: Pickup, feeding and other upgrades make it the main backpack after the SF3 ones.
goals.tip: Test pickup and feeding filters with cheap items before relying on them.
steps: Craft it and right-click it while held to open.
Store supplies and add upgrades in its upgrade slots.
Use the Open Backpack key while carrying or wearing it (fix conflicts in Controls).

goals.text: Move a full chest with Packing Tape
goals.hint: Tape a chest or machine to pick it up with everything inside.
goals.why: No emptying chests before a move.
steps: Craft Packing Tape and use it on a supported chest or storage block.
Break the wrapped block to pick up the package.
Place the package where you want it and unpack it. Unsure if a modded block works? Test it empty first.

goals.text: Carry a chest and its contents with a Chest Transporter
goals.hint: Right-click a chest with a Chest Transporter to carry it with its contents; right-click again to place it.
goals.why: No emptying chests before a move. Wood and iron transporters are enough.
goals.tip: Each move costs one use; better materials last longer.
steps: Craft a wooden Chest Transporter (planks + a stick), or an iron one for more uses.
Right-click a chest with it: chest and items go into the transporter.
Right-click a block to place the chest. Carrying slows you down.

goals.text: Climb with stepladders or Climbing Rope
goals.hint: Stepladders and climbing rope get you up walls.
goals.why: A cheap way up cliffs and into mines without building stairs.
steps: Craft stepladders or climbing rope.
Place stepladders against a wall and walk up. Place rope from the top: it hangs down.

goals.text: Build with Missing Pieces chairs, tables and wedges
goals.hint: Chairs, tables, wedges and corners for many blocks. Wood shapes come from the stonecutter.
goals.why: Detail plain blocks can't give, and you can sit on the chairs.
steps: Wood shapes: put planks in a stonecutter. Other shapes are crafted.
Place them like blocks; wedges and corners face you.
Right-click a chair to sit.

goals.text: Craft Graphite from Charcoal
goals.hint: 2 charcoal in the grid = 2 graphite.
goals.why: Graphite is black dye from charcoal: no squid hunting for ink.
steps: Smelt logs into charcoal.
Put 2 charcoal in the crafting grid for 2 graphite.

goals.text: Use Graphite to dye White Wool Black
goals.hint: Graphite works as a black dye.
goals.why: Black wool for builds and beds from charcoal alone.
steps: Put white wool and graphite in the crafting grid.
Graphite works in most recipes that take black dye.

goals.text: Activate a Waystone in a village
goals.hint: Right-click a village Waystone to save it; any Waystone can then send you there.
goals.why: The second travel upgrade: instant trips to every village you have visited.
steps: Find the tall stone pillar with a glowing top in a village.
Right-click it to activate it.
Right-click any activated waystone and pick a destination. Long trips cost up to 3 XP levels (1 per 500 blocks).

goals.text: Open a Loot Bag
goals.hint: Monsters sometimes drop Loot Bags; right-click one for a random reward.
goals.why: Extra loot from fights; rarer bags hold better items.
steps: Fight monsters until one drops a bag.
Right-click the bag.

obtain.lootbags:itemlootbag: Monsters sometimes drop Loot Bags; age rewards and bounties pay them too.

goals.text: Defeat a Special Mobs variant
goals.hint: Defeat a monster variant (brute, ninja, sniper, fire creeper...): they hit harder and drop extra loot.
goals.why: Variants and Infernal elites get more common the farther you go from spawn. Learn their tricks early.
steps: Fight monsters at night or in caves; variants have different names and colors.
Defeat one: the goal ticks itself.

mobs.where: Special Mobs turns some ordinary monsters into variants (brutes, ninjas, snipers, fire creepers...). They get more common far from spawn.

goals.text: Collect a Fallen Star
goals.hint: Fallen stars land at night; they craft Nyx Celestial gear.
goals.why: Nyx night events (Blood Moons and more) start after the first week; fallen stars craft the Celestial gear.
steps: Stay outdoors at night, watch for a falling light and pick up the star where it lands.

obtain.nyx:fallen_star: Fallen stars drop from the sky at night: stay outdoors, watch for the falling light and collect the star where it lands.

goals.text: Find a Hexxit World trinket
goals.hint: Hexxit loot has amulets, charms and rings with abilities like arrow or explosion immunity.
goals.why: Wear them in the accessory (Curios) slots: Aero Amulet stops arrows, Blast Charm stops explosions, Convection Ring lets you hover over lava.
steps: Loot Hexxit World ruins, Battle Towers and tumbleweeds.
Read the tooltip and wear it in an accessory slot.

goals.text: Raise your health with a Heart Container
goals.hint: 4 Heart Pieces (or glass panes around an eye of ender) = Heart Container: +1 heart.
goals.why: Permanent extra hearts make every later dungeon safer.
steps: Collect Heart Pieces from Hexxit dungeons and tumbleweeds, or craft a container from glass panes and an eye of ender.
Right-click the Heart Container for a heart. There is a cap; the game tells you when you reach it.

goals.text: Craft Tribal Hexxit Gear
goals.hint: Tribal armor needs a Hexical Diamond: fallen star + hexical essence + diamond.
goals.why: The first Hexxit Gear set, between iron and diamond.
steps: Get Hexical Essence from Battle Towers and bounty rewards, and a fallen star at night.
Craft a Hexical Diamond, then the armor pieces.

goals.text: Age 2 boss: defeat the Battle Tower Golem
goals.hint: The Battle Tower Golem opens Age 3 (Iron & Tinkering) for everyone on the server.
goals.why: When anyone on the server defeats the Battle Tower Golem, Age 3 opens for every player at once: its guide chapter, the reward bag and the decree of the age you finished. Age 3 brings Tinkers' tools and smeltery alloys, Create's first machines, Botania's Pure Daisy, Roots, Hatchery and Mystical Agriculture seeds.
goals.tip: The killer, or anyone within 64 blocks when it dies, opens the age for the whole server. Nothing to craft or hand in. /sf3ages lists every gate.
steps: Where: the roof of any Battle Tower (tall stone towers in the Overworld; several within 1,500 blocks of spawn).
Bring: iron armor, an iron or Tinkers weapon, a bow and arrows, food and blocks. Every floor below has spawners and chests.
Defeat it. Chat announces the new age and this goal ticks itself (ages open in order).
Drops: diamonds and redstone, plus the tower chests.

goals.text: Apply the Homestead Decree to a Bounty Board
goals.hint: Open a Bounty Board, click the Homestead tab on the left and place the decree in the empty slot: the page opens for good with Age 2 jobs.
goals.why: Opens the Homestead page: Age 2 jobs (items and kills) that pay one notch ahead. Optional: bounties never gate progression.
goals.tip: Right-clicking the board with the decree also works. Breaking the board returns it and every decree on it. The goal ticks when anyone opens the page.
steps: You get the Homestead Decree when Age 3 opens (every player gets one).
Right-click a Bounty Board to open it and click the Homestead tab (left edge).
Place the decree in the empty slot on that page. The page opens for good and gets 3 jobs at once, then a new one about every 3 minutes (up to 9).

goals.text: Optional: finish three Homestead bounties
goals.hint: Bounties are side jobs, never a gate. Use the Homestead Decree on a Bounty Board and hand in three jobs.
goals.why: Every player gets the Homestead Decree when Age 3 opens. On a board it offers Age 2 jobs (items and kills from every strand) that pay one notch ahead, never a skip. Skip a job you don't like and the board offers a new one. Bounties count for this decree until the next decree arrives.
steps: Craft a Bounty Board (6 planks + 3 paper) or use one in a village, and place it. The Bounty Boards page explains how jobs work.
Apply the Homestead Decree to its page on the board (the goal before this one).
Hand in three bounties; this goal counts them for you.
goals.tip: Lost your decree? Craft a copy: decree + paper (you keep the original). Old capstones still make their decree.

goals.text: Mine diamonds and make a diamond pickaxe
goals.hint: Diamonds are most common near Y -58; mine them with an iron pickaxe or better.
goals.why: A diamond pickaxe mines obsidian (Nether portal). Diamonds also make enchanting tables, the Twilight Forest portal and many machines.
goals.tip: Sifting gravel with a better mesh also gives diamonds.
steps: Bring an iron pickaxe, torches, food and a water bucket (turns lava into obsidian).
Dig down to about Y -58 (F3 shows your height) and branch-mine: 1x2 tunnels 3 blocks apart.
Caves near lava also have diamonds.
Craft a diamond pickaxe: 3 diamonds over 2 sticks.

goals.text: Build an Enchanting Table and enchant a tool
goals.hint: Diamonds, obsidian and a book make the table; 15 bookshelves around it unlock level 30 enchantments.
goals.why: Efficiency, Unbreaking and Protection make everything faster and safer; Fortune multiplies ores, Looting multiplies mob drops.
steps: Get obsidian: pour water on still lava and mine it with a diamond pickaxe.
Craft the enchanting table: 2 diamonds, 4 obsidian, 1 book.
Craft up to 15 bookshelves (planks + 3 books each). Place them 1 block from the table, level with it or one higher.
Put a tool and lapis in the table and pick an enchantment.

diagram.title: Bookshelf layout
diagram.view: Top view: 15 bookshelves with a 1-block gap around the table
diagram.note: Leave the gap free (no torches or carpet). Stack a second layer of shelves if you run out of floor space.

goals.text: Repair and combine enchantments on an Anvil
goals.hint: An anvil repairs tools, combines enchantments and renames items.
goals.why: Fix enchanted tools without losing the enchantments, and add enchanted books from villagers or loot.
steps: Craft an anvil: 3 iron blocks over 4 iron ingots.
Repair: a damaged tool + its material (or a second tool).
Enchant: a tool + an enchanted book.

goals.text: Craft and fire a Crucible, then melt Cobblestone into Lava
goals.hint: Smelt the unfired crucible, put it over a torch or lava and feed it cobblestone.
goals.why: Endless lava from cobblestone: fuel for furnaces and generators, and obsidian with water.
steps: Craft porcelain clay (clay + bone meal), then an unfired crucible; smelt it.
Put the crucible on a heat source: torch (slow), lava or fire (faster).
Right-click it with cobblestone; it melts into lava. Take it with a bucket.

goals.text: Make Obsidian in a Stone Barrel
goals.hint: Fill a stone barrel with lava, then right-click it with a water bucket.
goals.why: Renewable obsidian for portals, enchanting tables and obsidian chests.
steps: Craft a stone barrel.
Fill it with lava (bucket).
Right-click with a water bucket: it becomes obsidian.

goals.text: Craft the Tiny Progressions Cobblestone Generator
goals.hint: Makes cobblestone by itself; pull it out with a hopper or pipe.
goals.why: Endless cobblestone without water or lava, for hammers (gravel, sand, dust), crucibles (lava) and compressors.
steps: Craft the cobblestone generator.
Put a hopper or pipe under it into a chest or drawer.
Higher tiers are faster.

goals.text: Automate your Cobblestone with an Iron Cobblestone Generator
goals.hint: Iron, diamond, blaze and emerald tiers make cobblestone faster.
goals.why: More cobblestone per second for big sieving and crushing setups.
steps: Craft the iron tier from the basic generator and iron.
Swap it in. Later tiers: diamond, blaze, emerald.

goals.text: Compress Gravel and sift it in a Heavy Sieve
goals.hint: Craft 9 Gravel into one Compressed Gravel and sift it in a Heavy Sieve: one block gives nearly nine sifts of drops.
goals.why: Heavy Sieves were how SkyFactory 3 players sped up sifting before they had machines.
steps: Craft a Heavy Sieve (press G on it to see the recipe) and put a mesh in it.
Craft 9 Gravel, Sand, Dust or Dirt into one compressed block.
Right-click the Heavy Sieve with the compressed block, then keep right-clicking to sift.
In Age 4 the Auto Heavy Sieve does this for you.

goals.text: Make Grout and fire it into Seared Bricks
goals.hint: Grout = sand + gravel + clay; smelt it into seared bricks.
goals.why: Seared bricks build every Tinkers melter and smeltery.
steps: Craft grout from sand, gravel and clay.
Smelt grout into seared bricks.
Count bricks with the smeltery diagram first: controller, tank, drain, casting blocks and walls.

goals.text: Craft a Part Builder and a Tool Station
goals.hint: The Tinkers workshop: Blank Patterns, Stencil Table, Part Builder, Tool Station.
goals.why: Stencil Table: cuts patterns into part stencils. Part Builder: stencil + material = tool part. Tool Station: builds, repairs and upgrades tools.
goals.tip: SkyFactory 3's Tinkers with Tool Leveling: tools gain XP with use and get a free modifier slot each level.
steps: Craft Blank Patterns: 2 planks and 2 sticks in a checker = 4 patterns.
Pattern on planks = Stencil Table; on a log = Part Builder; on a Crafting Station = Tool Station.
Place them side by side: their screens share tabs. A Pattern Chest next to them stores stencils.

goals.text: Make a Tinkers' tool from a head, handle and binding
goals.hint: Make parts in the Part Builder from stencils, then build the tool in the Tool Station.
goals.why: Even a flint or copper Tinkers pickaxe repairs, levels up and can swap parts later.
goals.tip: Hover a part for its stats and traits. Metal parts are cast in the smeltery later.
steps: Stencil Table: pick a part (pick head, tool rod, binding) and take the stencil.
Part Builder: stencil + material (planks, cobblestone, flint, bone) = the part.
Tool Station: choose the tool, put the parts in the outlined slots, take the tool.

obtain.tconstruct:pickaxe: Tinker tools are assembled at a Tool Station from parts; the tool is not a fixed recipe.

goals.text: Build a Tinkers' Construct smeltery for processing ore
goals.hint: Seared bricks make the walls, controller, drain, tank and faucet. Melting ore gives extra metal.
goals.why: Melting raw ore gives more metal than smelting. The smeltery also casts tool parts and alloys bronze, rose gold and more.
goals.tip: The controller screen shows what is melting. There is no Tinkers book in this pack: hover the parts or use this guide.
steps: Build a floor of Seared Bricks, then walls one block high around the inside.
Put the Smeltery Controller (facing out), a Seared Drain and a Seared Tank in the walls.
Fill the tank with lava. The controller lights up when the structure is valid.
Put a Faucet on the outside of the drain and a Casting Table or Basin under it.
Put ores into the controller; right-click the faucet to pour metal into ingot casts.

diagram.title: Smallest smeltery
diagram.view: A 3x3 floor with a ring of walls on top; the middle stays empty.
diagram.note: Bigger smelteries (more walls, taller) melt more at once. The Faucet goes on the outside of the Drain.

goals.text: Cast a metal tool part and upgrade an existing tool with it
goals.hint: Pour molten metal from a faucet onto a Casting Table holding a cast.
goals.why: Metal parts (iron, cobalt, manyullyn) have far better stats. Gold casts are reusable.
steps: Put a part from the Part Builder (a wooden pick head works) on a Casting Table.
Pour 2 ingots of molten gold over it: the part becomes a reusable gold cast. Clay casts work once.
Melt the metal you want and pour it into the cast.
Swap that part of your tool for the metal part in the Tool Station.

obtain.tconstruct:clay_cast: Press a part or any item into a Casting Table with clay to make a cast.

goals.text: Make a Mattock
goals.hint: Shovel + axe in one tool: clears land fast.
goals.why: Digs dirt and chops wood at full speed.
steps: Pick the mattock in the Tool Station: axe head + shovel head + tool rod.
Make the parts in the Part Builder (or cast metal ones) and assemble them.

obtain.tconstruct:mattock: Tinker tools are assembled at a Tool Station from parts; the tool is not a fixed recipe.

goals.text: Add a modifier to a Tinkers' tool
goals.hint: Tool + modifier item in the Tool Station: redstone = Haste, lapis = Luck, quartz = Sharpness.
goals.why: Modifiers add speed, damage, Fortune and more. Tools start with free slots; Tool Leveling adds one per level.
goals.tip: Each tool level gives another slot. Tick this goal after applying a modifier.
steps: Check the tool's tooltip for free modifier slots.
Put the tool and the modifier items in the Tool Station: redstone = Haste, lapis = Luck, quartz = Sharpness, diamond or emerald = durability, obsidian Reinforcement = Reinforced.
Take the tool and check the modifier in its tooltip.

goals.text: Build a Tinkers' Sledge Hammer for mining three-by-three
goals.hint: A Sledge Hammer mines 3x3 per swing.
goals.why: Fast rooms, tunnels and quarries.
steps: Craft a Tool Forge: seared bricks, the Tool Station and metal blocks.
Make the large parts: hammer head, tough tool rod, two large plates.
Assemble the hammer in the Tool Forge (large tools need the forge).

obtain.tconstruct:hammer: Tinker tools are assembled at a Tool Station from parts; the tool is not a fixed recipe.

goals.text: Prepare a farming space for several crops
goals.hint: Hydrated farmland, light and fences keep a farm growing day and night.
goals.why: Many mods need different crops; one big farm keeps them all stocked.
steps: Till soil around water (one water block hydrates a 9x9 square).
Light it so crops grow at night.
Fence out animals.

goals.text: Make Fertilized Farmland with Hatchery manure
goals.hint: 8 chicken manure around dirt = Fertilized Dirt; hoe it into Fertilized Farmland.
goals.why: Fertilized dirt and farmland bonemeal crops and saplings on them at random: faster fields and tree farms.
steps: Collect chicken manure: chickens drop it over time; Nesting Pens collect it.
Craft Fertilized Dirt: 8 manure around a dirt block.
Hoe it into farmland and plant, or grow saplings on the dirt.

goals.text: Keep farmland wet with HydroGel
goals.hint: HydroGel hydrates nearby farmland like water.
goals.why: No water holes in your field.
steps: Craft HydroGel.
Place it where the water would go.

goals.text: Collect Inferium Essence from Inferium Ore or mobs
goals.hint: Mine Inferium Ore underground or kill mobs for Inferium Essence.
goals.why: Mystical Agriculture grows resources (iron, gold, diamonds) as crops; Inferium essence is its base currency.
steps: Mine Inferium Ore (stone with green flecks).
Kill mobs: they sometimes drop essence.

goals.text: Craft an Inferium Seed and start an Inferium Essence farm
goals.hint: Plant Inferium seeds; the essence they give upgrades into better essence.
goals.why: Better essence makes the resource seeds.
goals.tip: Upgrade with an Infusion Crystal, not a prosperity shard. JEI shows the recipes and crystal durability.
steps: Craft Inferium Seeds.
Plant them on farmland and harvest the essence.
4 Inferium Essence + an Infusion Crystal = Prudentium Essence; later tiers work the same way.

goals.text: Capture a Cow in a Jar
goals.hint: Lead a cow onto a Milk Jar and drop an anvil on it: endless milk.
goals.why: Endless milk for cakes, cooking and curing potion effects.
steps: Place a Milk Jar.
Lead a cow onto it (hold wheat).
Drop an anvil on the cow: it shrinks into the jar.

obtain.cookingforblockheads:cow_jar: Not crafted: lead a cow onto a Milk Jar and drop an anvil on it.

goals.text: Make a grass field away from your base for spawning animals
goals.hint: Animals spawn on lit grass: fence a large field.
goals.why: Animals to breed without hunting for them.
steps: Fence a lit grass field with open sky, in a biome where animals spawn.
Stay at a distance while the area is loaded (spawning also depends on mob caps).
No animals? Lead existing ones home and breed them.

goals.text: Analyze your chickens with a Chicken Analyzer
goals.hint: Resource chickens lay ores and materials. Breed two kinds together for new ones and check their stats with the Analyzer.
goals.why: SkyFactory 3 players bred resource chickens for renewable ores long before they had machines.
steps: Craft a Chicken Analyzer (press G on it to see the recipe).
Right-click a chicken with it to see its growth, gain and strength.
Breed your best chickens together; their chicks can be stronger.
Put them in a Henhouse next to collect eggs automatically.

goals.text: Collect eggs automatically with a Chickens Henhouse
goals.hint: Resource chickens lay items; a Henhouse with hay collects what chickens within 5 blocks lay.
goals.why: Chickens lay iron, gold, redstone, diamonds and more: renewable resources with no work.
steps: Breed two parent chickens for a new kind (JEI Breeding shows every pair). Throw colored eggs for dye chickens.
Craft a Henhouse (planks around a hay bale) and put hay bales in its top slot.
Chickens within 5 blocks lay into it; each hay bale lasts 100 items. Pull items out below with a hopper or pipe.
An Analyzer (egg + compass) shows growth, gain and strength: breed the best together.

goals.text: Hatch eggs in a Hatchery Nest and make a Lucky Egg
goals.hint: A Nest hatches eggs; the Lucky Egg Machine turns 24 eggs and 2 plastic into a Lucky Egg with a random prize.
goals.why: Nesting Pens collect eggs, feathers and manure; the Nest hatches eggs; Lucky Eggs roll a random prize.
steps: Craft a Nest (hay bales) and right-click it with an egg. A mob sitting on it or a powered block above speeds it up.
Put a chicken in a Nesting Pen with an Animal Net: it collects eggs, feathers and manure.
Craft the Lucky Egg Machine (planks, egg, iron blocks, circuit board), power it (40 RF/t) and feed it 24 eggs and 2 plastic.

goals.text: Grow corn and make popcorn
goals.hint: Plant kernels (from grass), harvest the cobs and cook them into roasted corn, popcorn or chowder.
goals.why: Another food crop used in many recipes.
steps: Break tall grass for corn kernels.
Plant them on farmland; corn grows two blocks tall.
Harvest the cobs and cook them.

obtain.sf3extras:corn_cob: Harvest grown corn. Plant kernels, which drop from tall grass.

goals.text: Build a Cooking Table kitchen
goals.hint: The Cooking Table lists every meal you can make from connected counters, fridges and jars.
goals.why: Shows what your stored ingredients can make and crafts it in one click.
steps: Craft the Cooking Table.
Place counters, a fridge and cabinets touching it; it reads their contents.

goals.text: Make a dark room away from your base for spawning mobs and collecting loot
goals.hint: Mobs spawn in the dark: funnel them into one kill spot.
goals.why: Bones, string, gunpowder, ender pearls and XP on tap.
steps: Build an enclosed dark room (light 0) at least 24 blocks from where you stand.
Push mobs into one corner with water streams.
Drop them 22 blocks (or into a kill chamber) so one hit kills them.

goals.text: Move and damage mobs with Dark Utilities plates
goals.hint: Vector plates push mobs; damage plates hurt them; filters choose which mobs.
goals.why: Move mobs without water and kill them while you're away.
steps: Craft vector plates and damage plates.
Steer mobs with vector plates; put damage plates at the kill spot.

goals.text: Build an underground workshop connected to your home
goals.hint: Dig a lit, enclosed workshop next to or under your home.
goals.why: Later ages add many machines; keep mobs and creepers away from them.
goals.tip: Light stops normal spawns; spawners and some modded mobs ignore light.
steps: Dig a room under or beside your home with space for machines and cables.
Light the floor, seal the entrances and keep dangerous machines apart.
Connect it to your home with stairs or an elevator.

goals.text: Travel between floors with Elevators
goals.hint: Stand on an elevator and jump to go up, sneak to go down.
goals.why: Instant travel between floors or down a mine shaft, no ladders or water.
steps: Craft two elevators (dye them any color).
Place them in one column, one per floor, with at least 2 air blocks above each.
Stand on one: jump to go up, sneak to go down.

goals.text: Obtain Andesite Alloy for your first Create components
goals.hint: 2 andesite + 2 iron nuggets in a square = andesite alloy (or mix them in a Mechanical Mixer).
goals.why: Create is the pack's mechanical tech; andesite alloy makes shafts, cogwheels, casings, belts and most early machines.
goals.tip: Hold W over any Create item for a Ponder scene that shows how it works.
steps: Mine andesite (grey stone in caves and mountains).
Craft 2 andesite + 2 iron nuggets in a square, or mix them in a Mechanical Mixer.

goals.text: Make Shafts and Cogwheels to carry rotation
goals.hint: Shafts and cogwheels carry rotation to Create machines.
goals.why: Create machines run on rotation from a source.
steps: Craft shafts (andesite alloy) and cogwheels (shaft + planks).
Shafts connect end to end; cogwheels connect side by side and change direction.

goals.text: Build a Create water-wheel workshop and connect a machine to it
goals.hint: Flowing water over a water wheel makes rotation.
goals.why: Free, endless rotation for your first Create machines.
steps: Craft a water wheel.
Put it on a shaft with flowing water running over it (side or top).
Run shafts and cogwheels to a machine. More wheels add their stress capacity.

goals.text: Use a Mechanical Press to make a metal sheet
goals.hint: An ingot on a depot under a turning press becomes a sheet.
goals.why: Many Create recipes need iron, copper and gold sheets. Over a basin, the press compacts items.
steps: Craft the press and a depot.
Put the press 2 blocks above the depot and give it rotation.
Drop an ingot on the depot.

goals.text: Connect two Shafts with a Mechanical Belt
goals.hint: Use a belt connector on two shafts; belts carry items and rotation.
goals.why: Belts move items between machines: the backbone of every Create line.
steps: Craft a belt connector (dried kelp).
Right-click one shaft, then another in line (up to 20 blocks apart).

goals.text: Wash gravel or crushed ore with an Encased Fan and water
goals.hint: A fan blowing through water washes items: gravel gives iron nuggets and flint.
goals.why: Crushed ore washes into extra nuggets; gravel into flint and iron nuggets (cheap renewable iron).
steps: Craft an encased fan and give it rotation.
Put water in front of it (flowing works).
Drop gravel or crushed ore into the air stream past the water.

goals.text: Combine ingredients with a Mechanical Mixer
goals.hint: A mixer above a basin combines items and fluids.
goals.why: Makes alloys, dough, chocolate and later brass.
steps: Place a basin, the mixer 2 blocks above it, and power the mixer.
Put ingredients in the basin; take outputs from it (or with a funnel).

goals.text: Automate a useful material with Create machinery
goals.hint: Build a Create line for a material you keep running out of.
goals.why: Teaches belts, funnels and machines, and saves hours later.
steps: Pick a target: iron sheets, cobblestone (mechanical drill on a cobble generator), gravel, bread.
Feed inputs with funnels or a mechanical arm; send outputs to a chest.

goals.text: Capture a structure with a Capsule
goals.hint: A Capsule packs a build into an item and unpacks it anywhere.
goals.why: Move a base or outpost in one go. Higher tiers need steel and vibrant alloy.
steps: Craft an iron capsule.
Use it on the block you want to capture.

goals.text: Place Redstone Paste on a wall or ceiling
goals.hint: Redstone Paste sticks to walls and ceilings where dust cannot.
goals.why: Run signals up walls and across ceilings, which dust can't. Circuits stay small and hidden.
steps: Craft redstone paste.
Right-click the side of a block or a ceiling: the paste sticks there.
It connects like dust to neighbors on the same face.

goals.text: Power a redstone device through a Redstone Paste connection
goals.hint: Run paste up a wall to a lamp or door.
goals.why: Tests wall wiring: a lever at the floor lights a lamp near the ceiling.
steps: Place a lever at the bottom of a wall.
Run paste from the lever up the wall to a redstone lamp.
Flip the lever: the lamp lights up.

goals.text: Craft a Charset redstone gate
goals.hint: A gate outputs at the front and reads its sides: NAND, NOR, XOR, RS latch and more.
goals.why: One small block replaces a redstone-torch contraption.
steps: Craft a gate.
Place it: front = output; the sides (and back) = inputs.

goals.text: Use a Charset NAND Gate in a powered redstone circuit
goals.hint: Wire two levers into a NAND gate's sides and a lamp to its front.
goals.why: NAND is ON unless both inputs are ON; every other gate can be built from NANDs.
steps: Place the gate; the front is the output.
Wire a lever to each side and a lamp to the front.
Both levers on: the lamp turns off. Any other combination keeps it on.

goals.text: Rotate a Charset Gate with the Charset Wrench
goals.hint: The wrench rotates any block with a facing.
goals.why: Fixes a gate or machine placed the wrong way without breaking it and losing its settings.
steps: Craft the Charset wrench.
Right-click the gate or machine to turn it.

goals.text: Store items in a Simple Barrel
goals.hint: A wooden barrel holds lots of one item.
goals.why: Cheap bulk storage for seeds, cobblestone or dirt.
steps: Craft a simple barrel.
Right-click with an item to store it; left-click takes a stack.

goals.text: Upgrade a drawer with a Storage Upgrade
goals.hint: Storage upgrades multiply a drawer's capacity.
goals.why: With upgrades one drawer holds thousands of items: a small wall stores a whole mine.
steps: Craft a storage upgrade (obsidian first, then iron, gold, diamond, emerald).
Open the drawer (sneak-right-click with an empty hand) and put the upgrade in an upgrade slot.

goals.text: Pair a Charset Key with a Charset Barrel
goals.hint: Right-click an unlocked barrel with a key to pair them.
goals.why: Keys and locks keep storage private on a shared server.
steps: Craft a key.
Right-click an unlocked Charset barrel with it.

goals.text: Lock a Charset Barrel and unlock it with the matching key
goals.hint: Use the paired key to lock and unlock the barrel; a Master Key can bypass its lock.
goals.why: The lock stops normal access; claimed chunks are the real base protection.
goals.tip: A Master Key opens any Charset barrel: the lock is not owner-only security.
steps: Pair a key with the barrel (previous goal).
Lock it with the key and check the barrel won't open.
Unlock it with the same key. Keep a spare key safe.

goals.text: Craft a Charset Master Key
goals.hint: The Master Key unlocks any locked Charset barrel.
goals.why: Recovers a barrel when the paired key is lost.
goals.tip: It bypasses every lock: keep it safe and rely on claims for protection.
steps: Craft the Master Key.
Use it on a locked Charset barrel.

goals.text: Craft and place a Charset Shelf
goals.hint: A shelf shows and stores six item stacks.
goals.why: Books, potions and trophies on display and in storage at once.
steps: Craft a shelf and place it on a wall or floor.
Right-click a slot to put the item in your hand there.

goals.text: Craft, wear and open a Charset Backpack
goals.hint: Right-click to wear it, then press B to open its 27 slots.
goals.why: 27 extra slots on your back.
steps: Craft the backpack.
Right-click to wear it; press B to open it.

goals.text: Upgrade a chest to an Obsidian Chest
goals.hint: Upgrade chests in order: wood -> iron -> gold -> diamond -> obsidian.
goals.why: More space: an obsidian chest holds 108 stacks and resists explosions. Four Obsidian Chests go into the Quantum DSU.
steps: Craft the chest upgrades (wood to iron, iron to gold, gold to diamond, diamond to obsidian).
Right-click a placed chest with the upgrade; the contents stay.

goals.text: Create a 16x16x16 Colossal Chest
goals.hint: Build a hollow cube of chest walls with a core in one wall; bigger cubes hold more.
goals.why: One giant chest: a 16x16x16 wooden one holds thousands of stacks.
goals.tip: Build a small one first to learn the structure.
steps: Get one Colossal Chest Core and wall blocks for a hollow 16x16x16 shell.
Build all six faces, floor and roof included; leave the inside empty.
Swap one wall block for the Core; add an Interface where automation connects.
Check the Core says the multiblock formed before filling it.

goals.text: Carry a Void Cup to delete junk
goals.hint: Items put in the Void Cup are destroyed.
goals.why: Delete cobblestone, dirt and junk instead of dropping it (dropped items lag the server).
steps: Craft a Void Cup.
Right-click to open it and put the junk in.

goals.text: Craft a Building Wand
goals.hint: Not Enough Wands: places a layer of blocks on a wall or floor in one click.
goals.why: Big builds go fast.
steps: Craft the wand.
Right-click the face of a wall: it adds a layer from your inventory. Costs a little XP.

goals.text: Chisel blocks into new designs
goals.hint: Put blocks in the chisel and pick a design.
goals.why: Hundreds of decorative stone, wood and glass variants.
steps: Craft the chisel.
Right-click to open it, put blocks in and click a design: the whole stack converts.

goals.text: Carve a block with Chisels & Bits
goals.hint: Left-click a block with a chisel to remove tiny bits; place bits with right-click.
goals.why: Details at 1/16 block: furniture, window frames, trims, statues.
steps: Place a chiselable block and hold a Chisels & Bits tool.
Pick its edit mode (tool tooltip or Controls).
Remove a small region, collect the bits, then place bits to build your design.
Keep bits in a Bit Bag or Bit Drawer.

goals.text: Make furniture at the Decobench
goals.hint: The Decomposer turns blocks into clay; the Decobench crafts decorations from it.
goals.why: Decocraft adds thousands of furniture and decoration models.
steps: Craft a Decomposer and a Decobench.
Put blocks in the Decomposer: they become decoration clay.
Spend the clay at the Decobench on furniture.

goals.text: Hang Fairy Lights between two fences
goals.hint: Right-click a fence with the lights, then another fence.
goals.why: String lights for paths, trees, markets and parties.
steps: Craft fairy lights.
Right-click a fence post, walk to another fence and right-click it.
Right-click the string with dyes or lights to change it.

obtain.fairylights:hanging_lights: Craft hanging lights from string, lights and a pattern of dye; JEI shows the pattern.

goals.text: Mix colors with Flat Colored Blocks
goals.hint: The paint mixer makes solid colored blocks.
goals.why: Exact colors for pixel art, signs and modern builds.
steps: Craft the paint mixer.
Combine dyes and blocks (JEI lists every color).

goals.text: Build ramps and floors with the Platformer
goals.hint: The platformer makes ramps, floors and railings from planks.
goals.why: Wooden ramps, floors and railings for bridges, docks and stairs.
steps: Craft the platformer.
Put planks in, pick a shape (ramp, floor, railing) and take the result.

goals.text: Decorate with Reliquia lanterns, candles and sword plinths
goals.hint: Colored iron and gold lanterns, candle holders and sword plinths.
goals.why: Colored lighting, and a plinth to display your best sword.
steps: Craft lanterns, candle holders or plinths.
Right-click a plinth with a sword to display it.

goals.text: Fire Porcelain and build with Porcelain Bricks
goals.hint: Smelt unfired porcelain; dye it or make bricks.
goals.why: White or dyed bricks; porcelain also makes buckets and faucets.
steps: Craft unfired porcelain (clay + bone meal).
Smelt it into porcelain.
Craft porcelain bricks (dye them if you like).

goals.text: Decorate with particle effect blocks
goals.hint: Particle blocks give off fire, smoke, hearts, notes or sparkles.
goals.why: Decoration for fountains, fireplaces, shops and parties.
steps: Craft a particle block.
Right-click it to cycle through the effects.

goals.text: Write a checklist on a Clipboard
goals.hint: A clipboard holds a to-do list you can tick off.
goals.why: Plans and shopping lists in-game.
steps: Craft a clipboard.
Right-click to open it and type a list.
Click a line to tick it off.

goals.text: Break glass without Silk Touch and collect Charset Glass Shards
goals.hint: Glass broken without Silk Touch drops shards.
goals.why: The shards craft back into glass.
steps: Break a glass block with your hand or a normal tool.
Pick up the shards that drop.

obtain.sf3extras:charset_glass_shard: Break a glass block without Silk Touch.

goals.text: Craft a Glass Block from three Glass Shards
goals.hint: 3 shards in a row = 1 glass block.
goals.why: Rebuilding windows never loses glass.
steps: Put three glass shards in a row in the crafting grid.

obtain.sf3extras:charset_glass_shard: Break a glass block without Silk Touch.

goals.text: Place a Charset Poster on a wall
goals.hint: Posters hang flat on a wall and show an item or map.
goals.why: Maps, items and art on a wall, without a frame.
steps: Craft a poster.
Place it on a solid wall and right-click it with an item or a map.

goals.text: Dye a minecart with a dye or Graphite
goals.hint: Right-click a minecart with a dye; the dye is not used up.
goals.why: Color-code minecarts by route.
steps: Place a minecart on a rail.
Right-click it with a dye or graphite; the dye is not used up.

goals.text: Knock back primed TNT without resetting its fuse
goals.hint: Hit lit TNT to push it away; the fuse keeps counting.
goals.why: A Charset tweak: hit lit TNT away from your walls.
steps: Far from your base, light a TNT block.
Hit the primed TNT: it flies away and the fuse keeps counting.

goals.text: Trigger the Zorro boost while falling toward a saddled horse
goals.hint: Fall more than two blocks onto a saddled horse and right-click it.
goals.why: A Charset stunt: land on your horse and it gets a speed boost.
steps: Tame and saddle a horse (saddles come from chests or fishing).
Jump from more than two blocks above it and right-click it while falling.

goals.text: Craft a Lexica Botania
goals.hint: Craft the Lexica (book + sapling): Botania's full manual. Mystical flowers give the petals.
goals.why: Botania is flower magic: mana, automation, tools and the Gaia Guardian boss.
steps: Find mystical flowers (glowing flowers in forests and plains) for petals.
Craft the Lexica from a book and a sapling.

goals.text: Craft a Petal Apothecary
goals.hint: Fill it with water, throw in petals and a seed: a special flower pops out.
goals.why: Every Botania flower, generating or functional, is made here.
steps: Craft the apothecary (cobblestone + petals).
Fill it with a water bucket.
Throw in a recipe's petals, then a seed.

goals.text: Create Livingwood and Livingrock with a Pure Daisy
goals.hint: Place logs or stone around a Pure Daisy and wait about a minute.
goals.why: Livingwood and livingrock build mana spreaders, pools and the runic altar.
steps: Make a Pure Daisy in the apothecary (4 white petals + seed).
Place it with logs or stone in the 8 blocks around it.
Wait about a minute.

diagram.title: Pure Daisy
diagram.view: Top view
diagram.note: Any mix of logs and stone works.

obtain.minecraft:oak_log: Chop any tree; every kind of log works.
obtain.minecraft:stone: Smelt cobblestone in a furnace, or mine stone with a Silk Touch pickaxe.
obtain.botania:special_flower: A functional flower is made by putting its petals and a mystical flower into a Petal Apothecary (see the Lexica Botania for the petal colors).

goals.text: Craft a Mortar and Pestle
goals.hint: Grind herbs in the Roots mortar into petal dust for spells.
goals.why: Petal dust is the spell ingredient of Roots.
goals.tip: Old Root, Verdant Sprig, Infernal Stem and Dragon's Eye drop from tall grass, crops, nether wart and chorus.
steps: Craft the Mortar (stone) and the Pestle.
Right-click the mortar with up to 8 ingredients of a spell (JEI or the Runic Tablet).
Right-click it with the pestle: they become petal dust.

goals.text: Burn incense in a Roots Brazier
goals.hint: A Brazier holds one incense item; light it with flint and steel and it burns for two minutes.
goals.why: Rituals bring rain, speed up crops, heal, repel monsters and more for a few minutes.
steps: Craft a Brazier (iron, string, cauldron).
Right-click it with the incense a ritual needs (JEI or the Runic Tablet).
Light it with flint and steel: it burns two minutes, long enough for a ritual next to it.

goals.text: Perform a ritual at the Roots Casting Altar
goals.hint: Three offerings on the altar, burning incense around it, then sneak-right-click the altar with an empty hand.
goals.why: Rituals change weather, heal, grow crops, summon creatures and make Roots items. The Runic Tablet (Roots guide) lists them.
steps: Craft the Casting Altar (verdant sprigs, poppy, rune stones, gold block) and the Runic Tablet.
Pick a ritual (JEI or the tablet): it lists three offerings, the incense and any standing stones.
Put the offerings on the altar, light braziers with the incense, build the standing stones if needed.
Sneak-right-click the altar with an empty hand: the ritual takes 10 seconds.

goals.text: Imbue a Roots staff with a spell
goals.hint: Stick + petal dust in the Imbuer = a staff that casts that spell.
goals.why: Spells heal, attack, grow plants and more at range. A staff has limited casts; the Crystal Staff holds several spells.
goals.tip: SkyFactory 3 Roots: no spell library, one spell per staff.
steps: Make a petal dust in the Mortar.
Craft the Imbuer (sticks, chiseled stone bricks); right-click a stick and the dust onto it.
After two seconds take the staff; right-click to cast. Terra (the bar above the hotbar) pays for it.

obtain.roots:staff: Made in the Imbuer: a stick and a petal dust become a one-spell staff.

goals.text: Explore a Trial Chamber and open an ominous vault
goals.hint: Trial chambers are copper-and-tuff rooms underground; ominous trials give Ominous Keys.
goals.why: Vaults hold enchanted books, diamonds and the Heavy Core for the Mace.
steps: Find one underground (copper and tuff rooms, often next to caves).
Beat the trial spawners for Trial Keys and open vaults.
Drink an Ominous Bottle (from raid captains) to start ominous trials for Ominous Keys.

goals.text: Craft a Mace and learn its falling attack
goals.hint: Heavy Core (ominous vaults) + Breeze Rod = Mace.
goals.why: The farther you fall before hitting, the harder it hits: huge damage on bosses.
steps: Open ominous vaults for a Heavy Core.
Kill Breezes in a trial chamber for Breeze Rods.
Craft the mace and jump onto enemies.

goals.text: Craft your own Waystone
goals.hint: A Warp Stone (emerald, ender pearls, purple dye) under stone bricks and over obsidian makes a Waystone.
goals.why: Link your base, mines and outposts to every village waystone.
steps: Craft a Warp Stone; on its own it also teleports you to a waystone.
Craft the Waystone, place it at your base and right-click to name it.

goals.text: Craft an Iron Bow
goals.hint: Iron bow: the second More Bows bow (gold, diamond and elemental come later).
goals.why: More damage than the stone bow, from plain iron.
steps: Craft the iron bow.

goals.text: Block attacks with an Apple Shield
goals.hint: Shields made from apples; golden and enchanted versions block more and last longer.
goals.why: A cheap shield line to upgrade as you go.
steps: Craft a red apple shield.
Hold it in your off-hand; right-click to block.
Upgrade to golden or enchanted golden apple shields later.

goals.text: Block with an Asgard Shield
goals.hint: Iron and gilded Asgard shields block (right-click) and parry.
goals.why: Sturdier than the vanilla shield; a well-timed block (Parry) knocks attackers back.
steps: Craft an iron shield.
Hold right-click to block.

goals.text: Defeat the Ferrous Wroughtnaut
goals.hint: A giant armored knight behind iron bars underground: hit its back after it swings.
goals.why: Drops the Wrought Axe (huge sweeping axe) and Wrought Helm: strong Age 3 gear.
steps: Find its chamber: a stone room with iron bars in caves or deep mineshafts.
Hit it to wake it. Dodge sideways when it raises its axe.
After a big swing its axe sticks in the ground: get behind it and hit the glowing spot on its back.
Pick up the Wrought Axe and the Wrought Helm.

mobs.where: Sleeps in a stone chamber behind iron bars deep underground. It wakes when you hit it; its weak spot is its back.

locate.label: Ferrous Wroughtnaut (if a hall is near)

goals.text: Defeat a Foliaath
goals.hint: A carnivorous jungle plant: let it snap, then hit it as it pulls back.
goals.why: Its seed grows a baby Foliaath you can plant as a base guard.
steps: Search jungle undergrowth: it hides among leaves.
Stay just out of reach, let it bite, then hit it.
Plant its seed where you want a guard.

obtain.mowziesmobs:foliaath_seed: Dropped by a Foliaath; plant it to grow a baby Foliaath that guards the spot.

mobs.where: A carnivorous plant hidden in jungle undergrowth. It snaps at anything that walks close; hit it when it pulls back.

goals.text: Defeat the Skeleton King
goals.hint: Fish's Undead Rising crypts and desert tombs, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks out, hide the Skeleton King.
goals.why: A Ring 1 boss: tests your Age 3 gear before the Nether.
steps: Explore crypts and desert tombs in the middle ring.
Clear the undead around it, then fight the king with a shield and healing food.

mobs.where: Rules the crypts and desert tombs of Fish's Undead Rising, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.

goals.text: Defeat a Chocolate Quest boss in the middle ring
goals.hint: Pirate ships and necromancer towers 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn end in a boss.
goals.why: CQR dungeons scale with distance: the middle ring gives Age 3-4 loot. The Pirate Captain drops his revolver, the Necromancer cursed bones.
steps: Go 1,500 to 4,000 blocks out (Ring Map page) and find a pirate ship or a tower.
Fight through the crew: CQR mobs use shields, potions and ranged attacks.
Defeat the captain on his ship or the necromancer at the top of his tower.

obtain.cqrepoured:captain_revolver: Dropped by the CQR Pirate Captain.

mobs.where: Commands a CQR pirate ship off the coast, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.

goals.text: Defeat a Giant from Ancient Beasts
goals.hint: Giants (294 HP) walk the plains and ruins of the middle ring.
goals.why: A big damage check for Age 3 gear; drops the Tough Glove.
steps: Look for a towering zombie in the middle ring.
Keep moving and hit its legs; bring food and a bow for when it gets close.

obtain.ancientbeasts:tough_glove: Dropped by the Ancient Beasts Giant.

mobs.where: A Giant (294 HP) that walks the plains and ruins 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.

goals.text: Age 3 boss: defeat an Elder Guardian (or the Ferrous Wroughtnaut or the Skeleton King)
goals.hint: An Elder Guardian opens Age 4 (Nether & Power) for everyone on the server.
goals.why: When anyone on the server defeats one of these bosses, Age 4 opens for every player at once: its guide chapter, the reward bag and the decree of the age you finished. Age 4 brings the Nether, Immersive Engineering steel, Ender IO, Actually Additions, Extra Utilities generators, Refined Storage, RFTools, Steve's Carts, Blood Magic, Industrial Foregoing and the first TaCZ guns.
goals.tip: The killer, or anyone within 64 blocks when it dies, opens the age for the whole server. Nothing to craft or hand in. /sf3ages lists every gate.
steps: Elder Guardian: inside an ocean monument. A cartographer villager sells an Ocean Explorer Map to one.
Ferrous Wroughtnaut: an underground hall closed with iron bars, found while caving.
Skeleton King: Fish's Undead Rising crypts and desert tombs, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.
Bring: a Tinkers or diamond weapon, good armor and food. Elder Guardian: milk against Mining Fatigue and a Water Breathing potion. Wroughtnaut: hit it from behind after it swings.
Defeat one. Chat announces the new age and this goal ticks itself (ages open in order).
Drops: Elder Guardian: wet sponges. Wroughtnaut: its axe and helmet. Skeleton King: its crown.

goals.text: Apply the Engineer Decree to a Bounty Board
goals.hint: Open a Bounty Board, click the Engineer tab on the left and place the decree in the empty slot: the page opens for good with Age 3 jobs.
goals.why: Opens the Engineer page: Age 3 jobs (items and kills) that pay one notch ahead. Optional: bounties never gate progression.
goals.tip: Right-clicking the board with the decree also works. Breaking the board returns it and every decree on it. The goal ticks when anyone opens the page.
steps: You get the Engineer Decree when Age 4 opens (every player gets one).
Right-click a Bounty Board to open it and click the Engineer tab (left edge).
Place the decree in the empty slot on that page. The page opens for good and gets 3 jobs at once, then a new one about every 3 minutes (up to 9).

goals.text: Optional: finish three Engineer bounties
goals.hint: Bounties are side jobs, never a gate. Use the Engineer Decree on a Bounty Board and hand in three jobs.
goals.why: Every player gets the Engineer Decree when Age 4 opens. On a board it offers Age 3 jobs (items and kills from every strand) that pay one notch ahead, never a skip. Skip a job you don't like and the board offers a new one. Bounties count for this decree until the next decree arrives.
steps: Craft a Bounty Board (6 planks + 3 paper) or use one in a village, and place it. The Bounty Boards page explains how jobs work.
Apply the Engineer Decree to its page on the board (the goal before this one).
Hand in three bounties; this goal counts them for you.
goals.tip: Lost your decree? Craft a copy: decree + paper (you keep the original). Old capstones still make their decree.

goals.text: Travel to the Nether
goals.hint: Build a 4x5 obsidian frame and light it with flint and steel.
goals.why: Blaze rods, quartz, glowstone, nether wart, wither skeletons and ancient debris: many mods need Nether materials.
goals.tip: Beds explode in the Nether: respawn with your Overworld bed.
steps: Get 10 obsidian and build the upright portal frame.
Light the inside with Flint and Steel.
Bring blocks, food and fire resistance if you have it. Mark the portal when you arrive.
Secure the return portal before exploring.

diagram.title: Nether portal
diagram.view: Side view (stand it upright)
diagram.note: The corners are optional. Light the empty middle with flint and steel.

obtain.minecraft:obsidian: Pour water onto still lava and mine it with a diamond pickaxe, or pour water into a Stone Barrel full of lava.

goals.text: Find a Nether Fortress and collect Blaze Rods
goals.hint: Fortresses are long dark-brick bridges; blazes spawn at their spawners.
goals.why: Blaze rods make brewing stands, blaze powder, eyes of ender and many machines. Wither skeletons (for the Wither) live in fortresses too.
steps: Travel along one axis (east or west) until you find dark red brick bridges.
Find a blaze spawner (a cage with fire) and fight blazes with a shield or bow.
Snowballs hurt blazes; fire resistance makes it much safer.

mobs.where: Blazes live in Nether Fortresses, around blaze spawners (a cage with a tiny spinning blaze inside). Bring fire resistance; snowballs hurt them. Carry a spawner home with a Diamond Chest Transporter for a blaze farm.

goals.text: Brew a Potion of Fire Resistance
