goals.why: Back to home, a farm or a portal from anywhere.
steps: Craft the dislocator.
Sneak-right-click to bind a location; right-click to teleport.

goals.text: Craft a Reliquary relic
goals.hint: Relics come from rare mob drops: the Fortune Coin pulls nearby items to you.
goals.why: Utility magic: magnets, mob charms that keep a mob type friendly, a handgun with special bullets.
steps: Collect rare drops: nebulous hearts (endermen), slime pearls (slimes), bat wings (bats). JEI shows each relic.
Craft the Fortune Coin (nebulous heart, gold nugget, slime pearl, bat wing); right-click to switch it on.

goals.text: Defeat an Infernal elite far from spawn
goals.hint: Infernal elites glow and carry modifiers (Vampire, Ghastly, Sapper...); more modifiers farther out.
goals.why: Elites drop enchanted gear. Rare near spawn; past 4,000 blocks and in the Twilight Forest they have 3 or 4 modifiers.
steps: Read the modifiers above an elite before you fight it.
Defeat one with 3 or more modifiers, then tick this goal.

goals.text: Craft an Ender Bow
goals.hint: Ender bow: the top More Bows bow (needs Age 4-5 materials).
goals.why: The best bow of the More Bows line.
steps: Craft the bow.

goals.text: Age 5 boss: defeat the Ender Dragon (or the Twilight Lich)
goals.hint: The Ender Dragon opens Age 6 (Mastery) for everyone on the server.
goals.why: When anyone on the server defeats one of these bosses, Age 6 opens for every player at once: its guide chapter, the reward bag and the decree of the age you finished. Age 6 brings the Gaia Guardian, the Chaos Guardian, Draconic awakened gear, the late Twilight bosses, big reactors and RFTools dimensions.
goals.tip: The killer, or anyone within 64 blocks when it dies, opens the age for the whole server. Nothing to craft or hand in. /sf3ages lists every gate.
steps: Ender Dragon: the End. Find a stronghold with Eyes of Ender and fill its portal.
Twilight Lich: the Lich Tower in the Twilight Forest, open once the Naga is beaten.
Bring: Age 5 gear, a bow or gun for the crystals and the Lich's clones, a water bucket, and slow falling or ender pearls for the End.
Defeat one. Chat announces the new age and this goal ticks itself (ages open in order).
Drops: Ender Dragon: the egg and lots of XP (dragon's breath with bottles). Lich: its trophy and a scepter.

goals.text: Apply the Realm Decree to a Bounty Board
goals.hint: Open a Bounty Board, click the Realm tab on the left and place the decree in the empty slot: the page opens for good with Age 5 jobs.
goals.why: Opens the Realm page: Age 5 jobs (items and kills) that pay one notch ahead. Optional: bounties never gate progression.
goals.tip: Right-clicking the board with the decree also works. Breaking the board returns it and every decree on it. The goal ticks when anyone opens the page.
steps: You get the Realm Decree when Age 6 opens (every player gets one).
Right-click a Bounty Board to open it and click the Realm tab (left edge).
Place the decree in the empty slot on that page. The page opens for good and gets 3 jobs at once, then a new one about every 3 minutes (up to 9).

goals.text: Optional: finish three Realm bounties
goals.hint: Bounties are side jobs, never a gate. Use the Realm Decree on a Bounty Board and hand in three jobs.
goals.why: Every player gets the Realm Decree when Age 6 opens. On a board it offers Age 5 jobs (items and kills from every strand) that pay one notch ahead, never a skip. Skip a job you don't like and the board offers a new one. Bounties count for this decree until the next decree arrives.
steps: Craft a Bounty Board (6 planks + 3 paper) or use one in a village, and place it. The Bounty Boards page explains how jobs work.
Apply the Realm Decree to its page on the board (the goal before this one).
Hand in three bounties; this goal counts them for you.
goals.tip: Lost your decree? Craft a copy: decree + paper (you keep the original). Old capstones still make their decree.

goals.text: Defeat the Hydra after completing the Fire Swamp prerequisite
goals.hint: Eat Meef Stroganoff first and bring fire resistance.
goals.why: Drops Fiery Blood for Fiery Ingots; one of the three branches to the Highlands.
steps: Eat Meef Stroganoff.
Find the Hydra lair in the Fire Swamp.
Hit its heads when they open their mouths.

mobs.where: Lives in its lair in the Fire Swamp. Opens after the Minoshroom; eat its Meef Stroganoff first or the swamp sets you on fire.

goals.text: Forge a Fiery Ingot
goals.hint: Fiery Blood (Hydra) or Fiery Tears (Ur-Ghast) + iron = Fiery Ingot.
goals.why: Fiery Ingots make Twilight gear that burns enemies and auto-smelts.
goals.tip: Fiery gear doesn't replace a Fire Resistance potion.
steps: Get Fiery Blood from the Hydra or Fiery Tears from the Ur-Ghast.
Combine it with iron (JEI recipe).
Check the gear's tooltip before relying on its protection.

goals.text: Complete Knight Phantom progression in the Dark Forest
goals.hint: Six Knight Phantoms guard the Goblin Knight Stronghold (opens after the Lich).
goals.why: Beating them opens the Dark Tower.
steps: Finish the Lich and bring a Twilight boss trophy to the Goblin Knight Stronghold.
Put the trophy on the entrance pedestal to open the shield.
Find and defeat all six Knight Phantoms.
Collect the reward and check the advancement before going to the Dark Tower.

obtain.twilightforest:knight_phantom_trophy: Dropped by the last Knight Phantom.

mobs.where: Six Knight Phantoms guard the trophy room of the Goblin Knight Stronghold in the Dark Forest. Opens after the Lich.

goals.text: Complete Ur-Ghast progression in the Dark Tower
goals.hint: Climb the Dark Tower (opens after the Knight Phantoms) and defeat the Ur-Ghast.
goals.why: Drops carminite; one of the three branches to the Highlands.
steps: Climb the Dark Tower (towerwood); careful with carminite reactors.
Defeat the Ur-Ghast at the top.

mobs.where: Floats at the top of the Dark Tower in the Dark Forest. Opens after the Knight Phantoms.

goals.text: Complete Alpha Yeti progression in the Snowy Forest
goals.hint: The Alpha Yeti lairs in a snowy cave (opens after the Lich).
goals.why: Opens the Glacier and the Aurora Palace.
steps: Find the Yeti lair (a snowy cave).
Defeat the Alpha Yeti; dodge the falling ice.

obtain.twilightforest:alpha_yeti_fur: Dropped by the Alpha Yeti in its lair in the Snowy Forest.

mobs.where: Lives in a cave lair in the Snowy Forest. Opens after the Lich.

goals.text: Defeat the Snow Queen in the Aurora Palace
goals.hint: The Aurora Palace is in the Glacier (opens after the Alpha Yeti).
goals.why: One of the three branches to the Highlands.
steps: Climb the Aurora Palace.
Defeat the Snow Queen and her ice shields.

mobs.where: Rules the top of the Aurora Palace in the Glacier. Opens after the Alpha Yeti.

goals.text: Complete all three major branches and enter the Highlands
goals.hint: Defeat the Hydra, the Ur-Ghast and the Snow Queen: the Highlands barrier drops.
goals.why: The last Twilight area: the Troll Caves and the Final Castle.
steps: Defeat the Hydra, the Ur-Ghast and the Snow Queen.
Enter the Highlands; the barrier is gone.

goals.text: Recover the Lamp of Cinders from the Troll Caves
goals.hint: The Lamp of Cinders is in the troll vault of the Highlands' Troll Caves.
goals.why: It burns away the thorns blocking the Final Castle.
steps: Finish the Hydra, Ur-Ghast and Snow Queen branches and explore the Highlands.
Find the Troll Caves and the giant cloud above them.
Get the Giant Pickaxe and dig into the protected vault.
Take the Lamp of Cinders and burn the thorns toward the Final Castle.

obtain.twilightforest:lamp_of_cinders: Found in the troll vault deep in the Troll Caves of the Highlands.

goals.text: Complete the Ritual of Gaia
goals.hint: Beacon with Gaia Pylons around it: use Terrasteel on the beacon, then defeat the Guardian.
goals.why: Gaia Spirits make Botania's best items: the Gaia ingot, the Ring of the Aesir and endgame flowers.
goals.tip: Gaia Spirits always drop and go into the Mastery Crown. An Elementium Axe kill can also drop its head (1 in 13), a trophy only.
steps: Build the beacon base and Gaia Pylons as shown (compare with the Lexica ritual preview).
Clear and flatten the arena around it.
Use a Terrasteel Ingot on the Beacon to summon the Guardian.
Stay in the arena, defeat it and collect the Gaia Spirits.

diagram.title: Gaia arena
diagram.view: Pylons four blocks out on each diagonal, one block higher than the beacon.
diagram.note: Keep 12 blocks around flat and 5 above clear.

mobs.where: You summon it: build the Gaia arena (a beacon on a 3x3 base and 4 Gaia Pylons) and right-click the beacon with a Terrasteel ingot (a Gaia ingot for the harder fight). It cannot be fought on Peaceful.

goals.text: Complete the Ritual of Gaia II
goals.hint: The harder Gaia fight: use a Gaia Ingot on the beacon.
goals.why: More Gaia spirits and rare loot like the Dice of Fate.
steps: Rebuild the arena.
Use a Gaia Ingot on the beacon instead of Terrasteel.

goals.text: Obtain a Master Blood Orb
goals.hint: A Weak Blood Shard in a tier 4 altar becomes the Master Blood Orb (25,000 LP).
goals.why: Tier 4 sigils and rituals and a much bigger LP network.
steps: Kill monsters with a Bound Sword (binding array) for Weak Blood Shards.
Build the tier 4 altar (Blood Magic book: Sanguine Scientiem) with Bloodstone capstones.
Put the shard in and keep the altar supplied: the craft takes 25,000 LP.
Right-click the orb to bind it, then leave it in the altar to fill.

obtain.bloodmagic:blood_shard_weak: Dropped by monsters killed with a Bound Sword (more with Looting).

goals.text: Automate LP with a Well of Suffering
goals.hint: The Well of Suffering ritual turns damage to mobs near the altar into LP.
goals.why: No more self-sacrifice: a mob farm next to the ritual fills the altar.
goals.tip: Runes of Sacrifice raise the LP per hit. Keep players out of the ritual area.
steps: Craft a Master Ritual Stone (obsidian, blank ritual stones, Magician's orb), ritual stones and a Weak Activation Crystal.
Set a Ritual Diviner to Well of Suffering and place the stones around the master stone next to the altar.
Right-click the master stone with the activation crystal (uses LP from your network).
Bring mobs into its range: a mob farm or spawner beside the altar keeps it going.

goals.text: Obtain the full Living Armor set
goals.hint: Living Armor levels up as you use it.
goals.why: Gains upgrades like speed and protection from what you do.
steps: Make Reagents of Binding in the Hellfire Forge.
Per piece: draw an array with Arcane Ashes, right-click it with the reagent, then with an iron helmet, chestplate, leggings or boots.
Wear all four pieces.

obtain.bloodmagic:living_armour_helmet: Binding array: draw a circle with Arcane Ashes, right-click it with a Reagent of Binding, then with the matching iron armor piece.
obtain.bloodmagic:living_armour_chest: Binding array: draw a circle with Arcane Ashes, right-click it with a Reagent of Binding, then with the matching iron armor piece.
obtain.bloodmagic:living_armour_legs: Binding array: draw a circle with Arcane Ashes, right-click it with a Reagent of Binding, then with the matching iron armor piece.
obtain.bloodmagic:living_armour_boots: Binding array: draw a circle with Arcane Ashes, right-click it with a Reagent of Binding, then with the matching iron armor piece.

goals.text: Train your Living Armor upgrades
goals.hint: Living Armor learns from what you do; a Training Bracelet blocks upgrades you don't want.
goals.why: Each piece levels upgrades (speed, step assist, arrow protection...) within an upgrade-point budget.
goals.tip: This version has no Living Station: upgrades come from use.
steps: Wear the full Living Armor set.
Do the matching activity: sprint for speed, take arrow hits for arrow protection, eat for knockback resistance.
Craft and wear a Training Bracelet to block unwanted upgrades.
Sneak over the chestplate tooltip for upgrades and points used.

goals.text: Automate the creation of Demonic Slates
goals.hint: Imbued slates in a tier 4 altar become demonic slates: automate the feed and output.
goals.why: Tier 5 needs demonic slates in bulk.
steps: Set up a tier 4 altar with enough LP.
Feed Imbued Slates in automatically.
Filter the extraction to pull out only Demonic Slates.
Test one craft first, then watch LP and output space.

goals.text: Create a Tier 5 Blood Altar
goals.hint: Build the tier 5 runes and capstones; confirm with a Divination Sigil.
goals.why: Unlocks the Archmage Blood Orb and Ethereal Slates.
steps: Follow the tier 5 rune layout in the Blood Magic guide.
Capstones: Hellforged Blocks (Hellfire Forge, JEI).
Check with a Divination Sigil that the altar is tier 5.
Have enough LP supply and capacity before tier 5 recipes.

goals.text: Build an Energy Core
goals.hint: A huge multiblock battery with four stabilizers around it.
goals.why: Stores millions to billions of FE.
steps: Place the Energy Core and right-click it: its screen can show a hologram build guide.
Build the required blocks around it.
Place 4 stabilizers in a cross, aimed at the core, then activate it.

goals.text: Fill a Draconic Energy Core
goals.hint: Pump power in until the core is full.
goals.why: Enough stored power to ride out any shortage.
goals.tip: Stored FE and production (FE/t) are different numbers.
steps: Build and activate an Energy Core of the tier you want to fill.
Build Energy Pylons with their glass blocks and link them to the core.
Set the feeding pylon to input and connect your generators.
Watch the stored energy rise until the core is full.

goals.text: Craft a Draconic Chestpiece
goals.hint: Fusion-craft Draconic armor: its shield absorbs damage while charged.
goals.why: A large damage shield; upgrades raise shield and energy.
steps: Get the Wyvern chestpiece, awakened draconium, an awakened core and a draconic energy core (JEI).
Fusion-craft the Draconic Chestpiece with Draconic-tier injectors.
Apply shield, recovery and energy upgrades (JEI: Draconic tool upgrades) and charge it.
Check shield and energy before a boss fight.

goals.text: Craft the Draconic Pickaxe, Axe, Shovel and Hoe
goals.hint: Fusion-craft Wyvern tools with awakened draconium into Draconic tools.
goals.why: Huge, fast mining areas while charged; dig-speed and dig-area upgrades push them further.
steps: Craft the Wyvern tools and the ingredients each JEI recipe asks for.
Fusion-craft the Draconic tools.
Apply dig-speed, dig-area and energy upgrades and charge them.
Test the mining area away from your base first.

goals.text: Craft a Draconic Staff of Power
goals.hint: The Staff of Power: Draconic mining tool and weapon in one.
goals.why: Huge area mining and top melee damage.
steps: Make the Draconic pickaxe, shovel and sword first.
Fusion-craft the staff from them.

goals.text: Create an Awakened Fusion Crafting Injector
goals.hint: Upgrade fusion injectors to Awakened for advanced recipes.
goals.why: High-tier fusion recipes need injectors of their tier (Awakened, then Chaotic).
steps: Upgrade a Basic injector to Wyvern, then fuse it with an awakened draconium block and a wyvern core into an Awakened injector (JEI).
Make as many as your next recipe needs.
Check the injector tier and energy cost before starting.

goals.text: Defeat the Chaos Guardian
goals.hint: The Chaos Guardian guards a chaos island far out in the End.
goals.why: Chaos shards make chaotic cores (top Draconic upgrades, reactor parts, the chaotic fusion injector), the reactor core and the Mastery Crown (one shard).
goals.tip: Late-game fight: a Wyvern chestpiece alone is not enough.
steps: Bring charged Draconic armor and weapons with shield, energy and speed upgrades, plus a way home.
Find a Chaos Island far out in the End, thousands of blocks from the center.
Break the chaos crystals first: they heal the Guardian.
After the win, take the reward and leave before the island is destroyed.

mobs.where: The Chaos Guardian lives on a chaos island far out in the End, thousands of blocks from the center, protected by chaos crystals.

goals.text: Defeat the Chaos Guardian four times
goals.hint: Each chaos island has its own Guardian: beat four.
goals.why: Chaos materials for more chaotic gear.
steps: Find four different Chaos Islands and defeat their Guardians.
Collect each reward.
Recharge and restock between fights; a cleared island doesn't count again.

goals.text: Create an actively cooled reactor from Extreme Reactors
goals.hint: Coolant ports turn water into steam for a turbine.
goals.why: Reactor heat becomes steam for turbine power; efficiency depends on the design.
steps: Build an actively cooled reactor from parts of one tier.
Fit coolant ports for water in and steam out and set their directions.
Connect a steady water supply and a turbine that takes the steam.
Start it, check coolant, steam and turbine output, and tune the reactor to the load.

goals.text: Create a turbine from Extreme Reactors
goals.hint: Turbines turn steam into lots of power.
goals.why: Turns reactor steam into big power.
steps: Build the turbine from one tier of parts: casing, Controller, rotor bearing, shaft, blades, induction coil (Extreme Reactors guide).
Add fluid ports (steam in, exhaust out) and a power output.
Fix the Controller's assembly messages before adding steam.
Supply steam, connect a load and tune the flow while watching rotor speed.

goals.text: Create the maximum size reactor
goals.hint: Expand a reinforced reactor to the server's maximum size.
goals.why: An optional engineering challenge: materials, assembly, cooling.
goals.tip: Basic and reinforced reactors have different limits; old SkyFactory sizes may not apply.
steps: Check the Extreme Reactors guide and the server's size limits for the tier.
Plan dimensions, rods, ports and moderators before gathering casing.
Expand in stages; check each with the Controller.
Test heat and fuel use before running it nonstop.

goals.text: Use Diamond blocks to cool a maximum-size reactor
goals.hint: Use diamond blocks as moderator in a maximum-size reactor and compare.
goals.why: Compare heat transfer and fuel efficiency against your previous layout.
goals.tip: More diamond doesn't always mean better: rod spacing and cooling matter.
steps: Build and validate the maximum-size reactor first.
Place diamond blocks around the fuel rods in the interior spaces.
Compare fuel use, temperature and output at the same load and rod settings.

goals.text: Build an Extra Utilities Nether Star Generator
goals.hint: Burn Nether Stars in the Netherstar Generator; send its FE to storage.
goals.why: Big power from Nether Stars. It makes FE, not Grid Power.
steps: Craft the Netherstar Generator and place it in a separate power area.
Connect FE cables and storage.
Insert a Nether Star; check output, fuel use and nearby effects before automating fuel.

goals.text: Generate sustained Grid Power with a Dragon Egg Mill
goals.hint: The Dragon Egg Mill gives a steady Grid Power (GP) supply.
goals.why: Runs GP utility devices. GP is not FE and is finite.
goals.tip: The mill gives 9,999 GP: that is not 9,999 FE/t and doesn't power FE machines.
steps: Craft and place the Dragon Egg Mill.
Meet its displayed requirements and check your GP total.
Connect your GP devices and keep them within the supply.

goals.text: Build a Solar Array Tier 4 Multiblock Structure
goals.hint: Build the tier 4 Environmental Tech solar array.
goals.why: Big daytime power from one controller.
steps: Craft the tier 4 controller, 40 tier-4 structure blocks, 81 solar cells and 8 modifiers.
Build it as shown.
Right-click the controller to check it.

diagram.title: Solar Array tier 4
diagram.view: K is the controller. Any tier 4-or-higher structure block works.

goals.text: Collect Ore from the Void with a Void Ore Miner Structure
goals.hint: An Environmental Tech multiblock that lasers ores out of the void.
goals.why: Endless ores.
steps: Craft the controller, structure blocks, machine bases, a laser core and a lens.
Build the layers (controller on top).
Power it and right-click the controller to check it. A colored lens favors ores of that color.

diagram.title: Void Ore Miner tier 1
diagram.view: K is the controller. Any tier 1-or-higher structure block works.
diagram.note: K = controller on top. The laser core points down through the lens.

goals.text: Sustain 1,000 FE/t
goals.hint: Generate 1,000 FE/t into a load and keep it stable.
goals.why: Enough for a full early workshop.
goals.tip: Production, not stored energy or nameplate capacity.
steps: Add generators and keep their fuel, cooling or daylight supplied.
Connect storage or a load that takes all of it (check cable and port limits).
Measure total delivered FE/t (don't count power twice as it passes through).
Hold it long enough to be stable, then tick the goal.

goals.text: Sustain 10,000 FE/t
goals.hint: Generate 10,000 FE/t into a load and keep it stable.
goals.why: Enough for big machine lines.
goals.tip: Production, not stored energy or nameplate capacity.

Measure total delivered FE/t (don't count power twice as it passes through).
Hold it long enough to be stable, then tick the goal.

goals.tip: Production, not stored energy or nameplate capacity. The biggest tiers are optional stretch goals.

Connect storage or a load that takes all of it (check cable and port limits).
Measure total delivered FE/t (don't count power twice as it passes through).

goals.text: Sustain 1 million FE/t
goals.hint: Generate 1 million FE/t into a load and keep it stable.
goals.why: Endgame power for Draconic crafting and big dimensions.
goals.tip: Production, not stored energy or nameplate capacity. The biggest tiers are optional stretch goals.

Connect storage or a load that takes all of it (check cable and port limits).
Measure total delivered FE/t (don't count power twice as it passes through).
Hold it long enough to be stable, then tick the goal.

goals.hint: Generate 1 billion FE/t into a load and keep it stable.
goals.why: The ultimate power challenge.
goals.tip: Production, not stored energy or nameplate capacity. The biggest tiers are optional stretch goals.

Connect storage or a load that takes all of it (check cable and port limits).
Measure total delivered FE/t (don't count power twice as it passes through).
Hold it long enough to be stable, then tick the goal.

goals.text: Open Dimlet Parcels and assemble a dimlet
goals.hint: Endermen drop Dimlet Parcels; their parts make dimlets at the Dimlet Workbench.
goals.why: Dimlets set what a custom dimension holds: terrain, biomes, blocks, sky, mobs.
steps: Hunt endermen: about 1 in 50 drops a Dimlet Parcel. Right-click it for dimlet parts.
Craft the Dimlet Workbench.
Combine a dimlet base, control circuit, type controller, memory unit, energy module and an essence into a dimlet.
Check its creation and upkeep costs before using it.

obtain.rftoolsdim:dimlet_base: Dimlet parts are not crafted: endermen sometimes drop Dimlet Parcels; right-click a parcel to open it into dimlet parts.

goals.text: Build a dimension, travel to it, and stay for at least 10 minutes
goals.hint: Write dimlets onto a tab, power the Dimension Builder, then travel by matter transmitter.
goals.why: Your own world: terrain, biomes, ores and sky by dimlet.
steps: Write the dimlets onto an Empty Dimension Tab in the Dimension Enscriber.
Put the tab in a powered Dimension Builder and wait for it to finish.
Keep the Builder supplied with enough FE to maintain the dimension.
Set up RFTools dialing and a matter transmitter; carry a charged way back.
Stay ten minutes while watching its power.

goals.text: Use an Absorber to make a custom block dimension
goals.hint: The Block Absorber learns a block for a block dimlet.
goals.why: A dimension made of the block you choose (allowed blocks and costs vary).
steps: Pick a block with a dimlet recipe in the Dimlet Workbench.
Place the Block Absorber on that block and let it charge fully.
Use the absorber in the dimlet recipe.
Add the dimlet to a dimension after checking its energy cost.

goals.text: Build a dimension using a rarity-4-or-higher dimlet
goals.hint: Use a dimlet of rarity 4 or higher in a working dimension.
goals.why: A challenge: rare components and their power costs.
goals.tip: Rarity belongs to each dimlet; worlds have no combined rarity score.
steps: Read dimlet tooltips and pick one with rarity 4+.
Get it through the Dimlet Workbench.
Write it onto a tab, build the dimension and keep it powered.
Travel there and check the feature.

goals.text: Use a Syringe and the RFTools Spawner to spawn an Ender Dragon
goals.hint: Fill a Syringe from the Ender Dragon and feed it to a powered RFTools Spawner with Matter Beamers.
goals.why: This version has no mob dimlets, so the old dragon-dimension challenge is a dragon spawn instead.
goals.tip: A spawned dragon breaks blocks and attacks players: spawn it far from bases, ideally in the End.
steps: Craft a Syringe and hit the Ender Dragon with it until full (see its tooltip).
Build an RFTools Spawner and put the syringe in it.
Feed it matter with Matter Beamers (link each to the spawner with a wrench). The dragon needs End Stone, bottles of enchanting and much other matter.
Give the spawner 100,000 RF per spawn and keep everyone at a safe distance.

goals.text: Build an Industrial Foregoing Supreme Machine Frame
goals.hint: Supreme frames need draconium ingots and a Hydra trophy.
goals.why: The top Industrial Foregoing tier: Draconic Evolution plus a Twilight boss.
steps: Defeat the Hydra for its trophy.
Smelt draconium ingots.
Dissolve plastic, an Advanced frame, netherite ingots, draconium, the Hydra trophy and ether gas.

goals.text: Craft a single Octuple Compressed Cobblestone Block
goals.hint: Over 43 million cobblestone in one block.
goals.why: A test of your automation.
steps: Automate a cobblestone generator into a compressor for each level.

goals.text: Build an XU2 Quantum Quarry
goals.hint: Quantum Quarry: activated Snow Globe, end stone and stoneburnt; six actuators and 20,000 RF per block run it.
goals.why: SkyFactory 3's endgame ore source: it mines a fresh world in its own dimension; stone can also give zinc, Yellorite, draconium, Aether and Twilight ores.
steps: Craft a Magical Snow Globe (needs a Nether Star) and carry it through 7 of its 12 biome types until it activates.
Craft the Quantum Quarry and six Quarry Actuators.
Put an actuator on every side of the quarry, power them (RF) and put a chest against an actuator for output.
An Efficiency book makes it faster; a desert Biome Marker makes it dig sand.

obtain.xu2blocks:magical_snow_globe: Craft it (it needs a Nether Star), then carry it through 7 of its 12 biome types until it activates.

goals.text: Get 20 different Chickens and automate resource collection
goals.hint: Breed up the chicken tree and keep 20 kinds laying into Henhouses.
goals.why: A collection challenge for chicken breeders.
steps: Breed up the tree (JEI Breeding shows each kind's parents).
Keep 20 kinds laying into Henhouses or Nesting Pens.

goals.text: Automate 20 crops with upgraded Ender IO Farming Stations
goals.hint: Farming Stations with Octadic Capacitors, tools and power, farming twenty crops.
goals.why: A farm-automation mastery build.
steps: Pick twenty crop types the Farming Station supports.
Build and power enough stations with Octadic Capacitors and their tools.
Supply seeds, keep replanting stock and collect each crop into labeled storage.
Check every crop is harvested and replanted without manual transfers.

goals.text: Craft a Master Infusion Crystal
goals.hint: An infusion crystal that never breaks.
goals.why: No more crafting infusion crystals for Mystical Agriculture.
steps: Craft it.

goals.text: Craft Supremium armor
goals.hint: Upgrade Mystical Agriculture armor to a full Supremium set.
goals.why: High-tier armor with augment choices.
steps: Follow the armor upgrade chain to Supremium in JEI.
Craft or upgrade all four pieces and wear the set.
Check augments and set effects before choosing upgrades.

goals.text: Craft a melee Tinkers' Weapon that does 20 damage or more
goals.hint: Strong head materials plus Sharpness (quartz) modifiers: reach 20 damage.
goals.why: A weapon for the Twilight and Aether bosses.
steps: Pick a weapon (cleaver, broadsword, longsword) and strong head materials; hover parts to compare attack.
Build it and add Sharpness (quartz) in the Tool Station; leveling gives more slots.
Check the attack-damage tooltip reaches 20.
Count the base value, not temporary potion effects.

obtain.tconstruct:cleaver: Tinker tools are assembled at a Tool Station from parts; the tool is not a fixed recipe.

goals.text: Create an unbreakable Tinkers' Tool
goals.hint: Reinforced V makes a Tinkers tool unbreakable.
goals.why: Never repair it again.
goals.tip: Five Reinforced use most of a fresh tool's slots: level it first.
steps: Craft Reinforcement modifiers: 8 obsidian around a cast.
Apply them one at a time in the Tool Station; each needs a free slot (level the tool for more).
At Reinforced V the tooltip says Unbreakable.

goals.text: Build any melee weapon that does 90 or more damage
goals.hint: Upgrade a late-game melee weapon to 90 attack damage.
goals.why: The ultimate weapon challenge.
goals.tip: Normal Tinkers modifier slots can't reach 90.
steps: Pick a late-game weapon with damage upgrades, e.g. a modular Draconic weapon.
Install its damage modules or modifiers within its capacity.
Charge it if needed and read its attack-damage tooltip.
Reach 90 on the weapon itself, not with temporary buffs.

goals.text: Jump between two tamed dragons while both are flying
goals.hint: A two-rider stunt: switch dragons in mid-air.
goals.why: For brave pilots (and friends).
goals.tip: Optional; it unlocks nothing.
steps: Get two tamed, saddled adult dragons and a second rider.
Practice mounting on the ground, then fly side by side over safe ground.
Get off one and onto the other while both fly.
Use fall protection.

goals.text: Craft the Mastery Crown
goals.hint: Awakened core + Gaia Spirit + chaos shard + paper: the guide's final trophy.
goals.why: The last goal. Every ingredient is guaranteed (crafted core, Gaia Guardian spirits, Chaos Guardian shards). Pays the Mastery reward once.
goals.tip: Nothing opens after it. It still crafts the Mastery Decree for optional bounties.
steps: Craft a Draconic awakened core.
Defeat a Gaia Guardian for Gaia Spirits.
Defeat the Chaos Guardian for a chaos shard.
Shapeless craft: awakened core + Gaia Spirit + chaos shard + paper. Right-click it for the reward.

goals.text: Apply the Mastery Decree to a Bounty Board
goals.hint: Open a Bounty Board, click the Mastery tab on the left and place the decree in the empty slot: the page opens for good with Age 6 jobs.
goals.why: Opens the Mastery page: Age 6 jobs (items and kills) that pay one notch ahead. Optional: bounties never gate progression.
goals.tip: Right-clicking the board with the decree also works. Breaking the board returns it and every decree on it. The goal ticks when anyone opens the page.
steps: Craft the Mastery Decree from the Mastery Crown (kept), paper, an ink sac and a gold nugget.
Right-click a Bounty Board to open it and click the Mastery tab (left edge).
Place the decree in the empty slot on that page. The page opens for good and gets 3 jobs at once, then a new one about every 3 minutes (up to 9).

goals.text: Optional: finish three Mastery bounties
goals.hint: Bounties are side jobs, never a gate. Use the Mastery Decree on a Bounty Board and hand in three jobs.
goals.why: Craft the Mastery Decree from the Mastery Crown (crown, paper, ink sac, gold nugget; you keep the crown). On a board it offers Age 6 jobs (items and kills from every strand) that pay one notch ahead, never a skip. Skip a job you don't like and the board offers a new one.
steps: Craft a Bounty Board (6 planks + 3 paper) or use one in a village, and place it. The Bounty Boards page explains how jobs work.
Apply the Mastery Decree to its page on the board (the goal before this one).
Hand in three bounties; this goal counts them for you.
goals.tip: Lost your decree? Craft a copy: decree + paper (you keep the original). Old capstones still make their decree.

goals.text: Complete every challenge in this book
goals.hint: Tick every goal in the book.
goals.why: A record of finishing every goal and optional challenge.
goals.tip: Ticks are shared on the server: only tick what your group has done.
steps: Done goals fold away in each list: what is left is what you still need.
Finish their objectives, including manual and cooperative ones.
This goal completes when every other goal is done.

pages.title: How Ages Open
pages.description: Each age opens for everyone when someone defeats its boss.
lines: Age 1 is open from day one and Age 2 opens with your first stone pickaxe and furnace. Every later age opens with a boss: when anyone on the server defeats it (the killer, or anyone within 64 blocks), the age opens for every player at once. Nothing to craft, hand in or find by luck.
Age 3 Iron & Tinkering: defeat the Battle Tower Golem. Battle Tower Golem: the roof of any Battle Tower, the tall stone towers in the Overworld; there are several within 1,500 blocks of spawn.

Age 4 Nether & Power: defeat an Elder Guardian (or the Ferrous Wroughtnaut or the Skeleton King). Elder Guardian: inside an ocean monument. A cartographer villager sells an Ocean Explorer Map that leads to one. Ferrous Wroughtnaut: an underground hall closed with iron bars, found while caving. Skeleton King: Fish's Undead Rising crypts and desert tombs, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.

Age 5 New Worlds: defeat the Frostmaw (or Barako or the Abyss Walker King). Frostmaw: snowy biomes, asleep in the open; it wakes when you hit it. Barako the Sun Chief: the chief of a Barakoa village in a savanna. Abyss Walker King: the top of an Abyss Walker castle, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.

Age 6 Mastery: defeat the Ender Dragon (or the Twilight Lich). Ender Dragon: the End. Find a stronghold with Eyes of Ender and fill its portal. Twilight Lich: the Lich Tower in the Twilight Forest, open once the Naga is beaten.

Finding the bosses: goals that mean finding something have a small Locate button at the right of their row (here: the age gate goals and every boss goal). Click it and Locate searches from where you stand, then an arrow and the distance at the top of your screen lead the way (also a waypoint on the FTB Chunks map). Battle Towers, ocean monuments, CQR dungeons (the Walker King's castle is a far one; Locate again from there for the next), the Lich Tower and the stronghold are found exactly; for the Frostmaw, Barako and the Skeleton King it finds the nearest snowy plains, savanna or desert. The Wroughtnaut's hall cannot be located: you find it while caving. Reference > Locate lists every other structure.
Opening an age gives every player the reward bag and the Bounty decree of the age just finished, ticks the age's boss goal and shows an advancement (press L, tab The Ages).
The only world lock is Age 5: the Twilight Forest and Aether portals stay shut until an Age 4 gate boss falls. Everything else (recipes, the Nether, the End) never waits on a gate.
Bounty boards are optional side jobs. Rare loot (dungeon chests, fallen stars, lucky drops) is a bonus, never a requirement.
Ages open in order: beat a later gate boss early and its age opens as soon as the age before it does. Type /sf3ages to see where your server stands.

pages.title: Bounty Boards
pages.description: Optional side jobs for loot and XP: boards, age pages, decrees and slips.
lines: Bounties are optional side jobs for extra loot and XP. No age, boss gate or recipe ever needs one: skip them, or skip any job you do not like.

Getting a board: craft a Bounty Board from 6 planks and 3 paper, or use one in a village. Right-click it to open it. Break it to move it: you get the board and every decree on it back, but the jobs on it are lost.
Pages: tabs down the left side of the board. Notices (basic jobs) is always open; Settler, Homestead, Engineer, Nether, Realm and Mastery each need their decree. Hover a tab to see what it needs.

Opening a page: click a locked tab and place that age's decree in the empty slot (or right-click the board with the decree). The decree stays in the board and the page opens for good with 3 jobs. Each opened page is an advancement and ticks its guide goal.

Getting decrees: craft the Settler Decree from a Bounty Board (kept), 2 paper, 2 ink sacs, a feather and a gold nugget. Homestead to Realm: every player gets the decree of the age just finished when the next age opens. Craft the Mastery Decree from the Mastery Crown. A decree and a paper make a copy for a second board.

Jobs: every open page gets its own jobs from that age's list, a new one about every 3 minutes, up to 9 per page (when it is full, an old one makes room). Rewards are at most one age ahead. A job nobody takes leaves the board after an hour.
Taking a job: click a bounty slip to take it. It says what to bring (one or two kinds of items) and which mobs to kill. Kills count when you land the killing blow with the slip in your inventory.

Variants count: a slip for "Any Apple Pie", "Any Wool" or "Any Coal or Charcoal" takes every kind of that item, mixed as you like (one apple pie of each kind adds up). Renamed or damaged items count too.
No time limit: a slip you take never expires. Keep it in your inventory (or a chest) as long as you like. Do not put it back on a board: slips on a board are cleared after an hour.
Cashing in: right-click any Bounty Board with the slip in your hand once you have everything (any page, any board). The items are taken and you get the rewards plus XP.
Rarity: a slip is common, uncommon, rare or epic (each step up is a 1 in 3 chance). Rarer slips are worth more (up to 1.6 times) and give more XP: 6, 10, 14 or 24 points.
The Bounties page (Reference) counts the jobs you finish for each decree; the optional decree goals tick themselves after three.

pages.title: Ring Map
pages.description: How far from spawn decides how hard the world is.
lines: The overworld is your difficulty dial. The farther you walk from the world spawn, the harder the dungeons, the better the loot and the nastier the mobs. Pick your challenge by choosing how far to travel.

Ring 0 (0 to 1,500 blocks): Ages 1 and 2. Hexxit World ruins, Battle Towers (a Golem on every roof), small Roguelike dungeons, huts, Secret Rooms, villages with bounty boards. Loot is Age 1-2 gear and seeds.
Ring 1 (1,500 to 4,000 blocks): Ages 3 and 4. Tier 1 and 2 bandit camps and towers, deeper Roguelike levels, trap dungeons and mineshafts. Loot is Age 3-4: steel, Psi bullets, Hexxit sets.
Ring 2 (4,000+ blocks): Ages 5 and 6. Tier 3 castles and bosses, the deepest Roguelike levels, ancient beast lairs. Loot is Age 5-6.
Other places have a fixed level: the Nether and End follow the vanilla order, the Twilight Forest and the Aether are Age 5, and ocean-floor Lunkertooth ruins are an Age 4 side trip.
Mobs follow the rings too: infernal elites with more modifiers appear far from spawn and in the Twilight Forest, and the Nyx blood moons only start once you have been to the Nether.
The ring dungeons are optional: loot and gear, never a gate. The age gates are bosses (see How Ages Open).

pages.title: Bestiary
pages.description: Every boss: where, how ready you should be, and what it unlocks.
lines: Battle Tower Golem (Age 2): top of a stone tower within 1,500 blocks. Bring iron gear and a bow. Drops 6 to 12 diamonds and redstone.
Elder Guardian (Age 3): ocean monuments; a cartographer sells the map. Mining fatigue: bring milk. Defeating it opens Age 4 for everyone; drops wet sponges.
Lunkertooth (Age 4): ambushes divers in ocean-floor ruins. Drops eggs and Esca.
Ferrous Wroughtnaut and Foliaath (Age 3, Mowzie's): the armored knight sleeps behind iron bars underground (hit its back after a swing); the Foliaath hides in jungle undergrowth.
Skeleton King, CQR Pirate Captain and Necromancer, Ancient Beasts Giant (Age 3): the middle ring, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks out. Bring Age 3 gear and healing food.
Barako and Frostmaw (Age 4, Mowzie's), Abyss Walker King (CQR), Vessel and Harbinger (Age 4): savanna villages, snowy biomes and the middle ring (1,500 to 4,000 blocks).
Ender Calamity (Age 5, CQR): its own arena in the End, after the Dragon. Infernal elites with 3-4 modifiers roam the far ring and the Twilight Forest.
Wither (Age 5): built from soul sand and three skulls from Nether fortresses. Bring ranged damage and strong armor. Drops the Nether Star: beacons, Draconic fusion and more.
Ender Dragon (Age 5): the End. Crystals first, then the dragon. Drops dragon breath and the egg that Dragon Mounts can hatch.

Twilight Forest bosses: Naga, Lich and Minoshroom (Age 5), then Hydra, Knight Phantoms, Ur-Ghast, Alpha Yeti and Snow Queen (Age 6); each opens the next. The Lich opens Age 6 (as does the Ender Dragon); trophies feed Industrial Foregoing supreme frames.
Aether bosses (Age 5): Slider (bronze dungeon, pickaxe), Valkyrie Queen (silver), Sun Spirit (gold). They drop dungeon keys; the silver dungeon's Valkyries drop the victory medals the Queen asks for.
Gaia Guardian I and II (Age 6): the Botania ritual. Drops Gaia Spirits every time (one goes into the Mastery Crown); an Elementium Axe kill can also drop its head, a trophy only.
Chaos Guardian (Age 6): Draconic Evolution's island. Drops chaos shards; one goes into the Mastery Crown.

Gear by age: Age 2 iron or Tribal Hexxit gear; Age 3 Tinkers, Hexxit sets and Mowzie's gear; Age 4 steel, dark steel, Psi, pistols and rifles; Age 5 Wyvern gear and heavy weapons from Twilight and Aether materials; Age 6 Draconic.

pages.title: Trade Routes
pages.description: How one mod feeds another: the links that tie the pack together.
lines: Mo' Creatures hide and fur work as leather for the basic Iron Backpack, and a Sophisticated Backpack is built on an Iron Backpack.
IE steel opens the Create crushing wheel and the first TaCZ pistols; IE electrum opens Create brass and the precision mechanism.
Ender IO dark steel, electrical steel and vibrant alloy are the middle gate: Industrial Foregoing advanced frames, TaCZ rifles and attachments, airship propeller bearings and gold capsules.
Twilight and Aether materials are catalysts: knightmetal and zanite for heavy guns, ambrosium for levitite (airship lift), a Hydra trophy and draconium for Industrial Foregoing supreme frames.

Bring a block home from another dimension and sieve it: Aether dirt gives ambrosium and zanite, quicksoil gives gravitite, Twilight maze stone gives raw ironwood. The trip comes first, the automation second.
Aether dirt can be made again from skyroot leaves in a barrel with water, once you own the first stack.
Soul Shards and Ender IO soul vials are one system: both feed spawners. Blood Magic and the Bound Sword drop Weak Blood Shards for the Master Blood Orb.

Each automation method has its niche: sieves and the IE excavator are the early bulk ores, the Industrial Foregoing laser drill (lenses need Ender IO steel) is the focused rare-ore machine, the XU2 Quantum Quarry is the late random-world ore (now with modded and dimension finds), and the Botania Orechid is the mana-only route (slow, but no power).

Steve Carts is for tunnelling and rail farms, Mystical Agriculture is the passive essence chain, the Blood Magic alchemy table is the cheap early doubling, and the Arc Furnace is for alloys, not for multiplying ore.
Raw ore doubles like the old ore blocks in the IE crusher, the Ender IO SAG mill and the Actually Additions crusher; Create gives 1.75.
Ages open with bosses, not with crafted items: see How Ages Open. Old capstones are keepsakes that still make their Bounty decree.
Bounty boards are optional side jobs: they ask for items and kills from every strand of an age and pay one notch ahead, never a skip.

pages.title: Story: the Settlers
pages.description: A short story page for age 1.
lines: A torch, a coffee and a slice of toast. The land is quiet, the nights are not. People before you left books in the ruins: read them, and learn where the first villages stand.

pages.title: Story: the Homestead
pages.description: A short story page for age 2.
lines: Smoke rises over your fields. Towers of old stone watch the plains, and a golem sleeps on top of each. The village board asks for bread, bricks and bravery.

pages.title: Story: Iron and Gears
pages.description: A short story page for age 3.
lines: Iron and gears change everything. Smelteries roar, water wheels turn and the first machines start to hum. Far out, past the old roads, castles of bandits and ruins of something older wait.

pages.title: Story: Below and Beyond
pages.description: A short story page for age 4.
lines: The Nether answers your fire with fire. Steel, alloys, conduits and generators power a base that never sleeps, while in the dark water something with a lantern for a lure waits for divers.

pages.title: Story: New Worlds
pages.description: A short story page for age 5.
lines: Doors open to places that have no right to exist: a forest that never sees day and islands in the sky. Reactors hum at home while the old lords out there will not yield to anything you have built so far.

pages.title: Story: Mastery
pages.description: A short story page for age 6.
lines: The deepest Twilight lords still wait in the swamp, the dark tower and the glacier. Beyond them only two guardians remain, one of mana and one of chaos. When both bow, the crown is yours and the world, at last, is yours to shape.
